title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS 72nd NATIONAL FILM AWARDS; CONFERS DADASAHEB PHALKE AWARD ON SHRI ANANT NAG
text:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu presented the 72nd National Film Awards at a function held at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, Gujarat today (September 22, 2026). She also conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024 upon veteran actor Shri Anant Nag in recognition of his outstanding contribution to Indian cinema.
Speaking on the occasion, the President congratulated all the award winners who, through their exceptional talent and hard work have carved a niche for themselves at the national level. She expressed happiness that Shri Anant Nag has been honoured with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. She said that his acting in films represents a synthesis of the finest elements of theatre and cinema. He is renowned for his natural, restrained and authentic performances. He sets an ideal example for future generations of artists.
The President said that the image of India is reflected in films across all languages and regions. Indian cinema embodies the dreams, traditions, and struggles of the Indian people, as well as the possibilities for the future. She was happy to note that the ceremony to honour outstanding films is being held on the premises of the Statue of Unity, near the Wall of Unity. She said that the occasion seemed to evoke the presence of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the architect of India’s unity, as though he were himself blessing this festival celebrating the country’s cultural unity.
The President appreciated all the award-winning films. She said that the film ‘Article 370’ presents a vivid account of the serious challenges facing the country's unity and their solutions. The non-feature film ‘Bhangaar’ expresses unseen dimensions related to life and death, meaning and meaninglessness. ‘Swatantrya Veer Savarkar’ is an artistic tribute to the extraordinary life story of Veer Savarkar Ji. The film ‘Bhakshak’ raises societal awareness about the extremely serious issue of women's safety. National-level recognition of the Santhali film ‘Angen’ has provided encouragement to an outstanding film and it has also fostered cultural diversity and social inclusion.
The President commended the jury members for selecting films that address significant issues concerning society and the nation. She said that women's participation in every regional jury should be ensured. She underlined that in any field, a holistic human perspective can be formed by incorporating the viewpoint of women.
The President said that maintaining a sense of respect and sensitivity towards every member of the team should be an integral part of the film industry's work culture. She urged the key representatives of the creative economy to ensure that the workers, small-scale artists, assistants and strugglers receive due respect and social security.
The President said that the popular film artists possess immense potential to influence the people of the country, especially the youth. When successful film artists speak about the benefits of a disciplined lifestyle, millions of children and young people emulate them. She urged celebrities not to endorse products that are harmful to healt h. She said that a true star is one who spreads light, not darkness.

title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE VALEDICTORY SESSION OF THE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON ‘THE FUTURE OF ENVIRONMENT AND CLIMATE DYNAMICS’
text:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the valedictory session of the International Conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’, organized by the National Green Tribunal, in New Delhi today (September 20, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that climate change creates imbalances across multiple levels of human existence. Issues such as biodiversity loss, water stress and land degradation are deeply intertwined with it. Climate change is also having serious repercussions on food security, health, and livelihoods.
The President said that a well-structured framework of policies and actions is essential to effectively address such a complex challenge. The framework must ensure the active participation of not only governments and legal experts but also the communities most affected by climate change. Special sensitivity towards the needs of rural and forest-dwelling societies, small farmers, women, and other vulnerable communities is crucial, as they bear the brunt of natural disasters.
The President underlined that traditional knowledge systems, along with the practices and lived experiences of local communities, play a vital role in enhancing climate adaptation capacity. She said that we must strengthen climate resilience through people-centric and community-based adaptation approaches rooted in traditional knowledge. She stated that sustainable afforestation can also play a significant role in enhancing climate resilience. Afforestation efforts that nurture biodiversity and are aligned with local conditions can be instrumental in this regard. She stated that the true objective of sustainable afforestation is not merely planting trees, but rather restoring healthy and self-sustaining ecosystems.
The President said that developing countries should chart a path that enhances resilience while maintaining the pace of development. Commitments to responsible climate action must align with the country's development needs and economic aspirations. They must also be technically feasible. She was happy to note that many such aspects have been discussed at the Conference.
The President said that India has done commendable work in fostering environmental awareness by engaging common citizens, especially the youth. The Government of India's 'Mission LiFE' initiative has demonstrated that meaningful strides towards ecological restoration can be achieved through public participation and community ownership.
The President appreciated the National Green Tribunal for bringing experts, judges, jurists, and key stakeholders from various countries, who are active in environmental issues, on one platform. She expressed confidence that deliberations and action plans from this Conference will contribute to paving the way for building climate-resilient societies, grounded in inclusive policies and effective actions.

title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA TO VISIT GUJARAT FROM SEPTEMBER 21 TO 23
text:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu will visit Gujarat from September 21 to 23, 2026.
On September 22, the President will grace the presentation ceremony of the 72nd National Film Awards at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia.
On September 23, the President will grace the 75th annual convocation ceremony of the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda at Vadodara. On the same day, she will launch Brahma Kumaris’ campaign ‘Spiritual Awakening for World Renewal’ and inaugurate the ‘Global Spiritual Palace’ Retreat Centre at Vadodara. She will also virtually launch the campaign ‘Youth for Viksit Bharat: Awakening Inner Strength for Nation Building’ of Brahma Kumaris Nadiad on the occasion.

title: PRESIDENT OF THE ISLAMIC REPUBLIC OF IRAN MEETS THE PRESIDENT
text:
His Excellency Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian, President of the Islamic Republic of Iran, met President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (September 12, 2026).
Welcoming President Pezeshkian on his first visit to India, the President expressed appreciation for the support extended by Iran during India's BRICS presidency.
The two leaders discussed the long-standing bonds of friendship between Iran and India, including our strong cultural and people-to-people ties. The President reiterated India's commitment to the pursuit of enduring peace in the region, and called for conflicts to be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.

title: PRINCE RAHIM AGA KHAN V CALLS ON THE PRESIDENT
text:
His Highness Prince Rahim Aga Khan V called on the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (September 10, 2026).
Welcoming him on his first official visit to India since assuming the role of the Aga Khan, the President offered her condolences on the passing of his father, the late Aga Khan IV. She said that in India, we regard the Aga Khan IV and the work undertaken by the Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN) with great respect and affection.
The President appreciated the projects implemented in India by Aga Khan Development Network in areas such as water and sanitation, education, maternal health, urban redevelopment, women's empowerment, and employment generation. She said that these projects are excellent examples of public-private partnerships and demonstrate how non-profit organizations, working in partnership with the government, can improve people's quality of life.

title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA CONFERS NATIONAL AWARDS ON TEACHERS
text:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu conferred National Awards on teachers from across the country at a function held in New Delhi today (September 5, 2026) on Teachers’ Day.
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that education is the most effective means of realizing the ideal of equality of opportunity enshrined in our Constitution.  She said that the achievement of negligible primary school dropout rate, has been made possible through the efforts of teachers. She appreciated all the teachers for this national success.
The President said that school education forms the foundation of education system. While knowledge and skills can be acquired at any time, imparting lessons in good conduct during childhood proves far more effective. By diligently focusing on the intellectual, physical, and moral development of children in the early grades, our teachers can prepare future generations of excellent students and dutiful citizens.
The President underlined that many students come from economically disadvantaged families; some are first-generation learners; others transition from ordinary village schools to large city schools; some are naturally shy; some possess immense talent but lack self-confidence; and some are children with special needs. It is the special responsibility of teachers to instill confidence in them and uplift all such students who, for any reason, feel a sense of inadequacy.
The President said that academic excellence, skill development, and entrepreneurship hold immense importance in the country's development. Establishing India as the skill capital of the world, and transforming it into a knowledge superpower, is among our national priorities.
The President said that we are moving towards the goal of building a Viksit Bharat and this goal can be achieved only through a world-class education system. Our teachers breathe life into the education system. We must strive to ensure that not even a single student in our country is deprived of opportunities for quality education. She emphasised that our teachers should instill knowledge, inspiration, morality, and sensitivity in all students through their affection and dedication.

title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA’S GREETINGS ON THE EVE OF TEACHERS’ DAY
text:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu has greeted teachers across the country on the eve of Teachers’ Day.
In a message, the President has said, “On the occasion of Teachers’ Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings to all our teachers across the country. Teachers’ Day is observed to mark the birth anniversary of the former President of India, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan who was a great author and philosopher. He was also an extraordinary teacher. On this occasion, I pay my humble tributes to him.
Teachers, through their guidance and mentorship, play a vital role in nurturing talent and strengthening character. It is their duty to guide students to become good human beings.  A dedicated and caring teacher can recognise the unique potential of students, serve as a source of inspiration and encourage them to strive for excellence.
The teachers should continually update their knowledge, embrace technology and adopt innovative teaching methods. They should promote independent thinking and cultivate a spirit of enquiry among students.
I express my gratitude to all the dedicated teachers for their contribution. I wish that all teachers nurture enlightened generations who will take the nation to greater heights”.

title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA'S GREETINGS ON THE EVE OF JANMASHTAMI
text:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu in her message on the eve of Janmashtami says: -
“On the auspicious occasion of Janmashtami, I extend my heartfelt greetings and best wishes to all Indians living in India and abroad.
The life and teachings of Bhagwan Shri Krishna breathe new life into Indian cultural and philosophical heritage. Bhagwan Shri Krishna showed the path of truth, righteousness, justice, compassion and selfless service. His teachings, embodied in Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, remain an eternal source of inspiration for humanity to make prudent decisions during difficult times and to remain steadfast in moral values.
The sacred festival of Janmashtami inspires us to uphold the spirit of harmony, and devotion to duty and service.
On this auspicious occasion, let us resolve to follow the ideals of Bhagwan Shri Krishna and continue working tirelessly towards building an inclusive and developed India”.

title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurates 9th India International Water Week 2026 at Bharat Mandapam
text:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the 9th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The five-day event, being organised by the Ministry of Jal Shakti from September 22 to 26, is centred on the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management.”
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the 9th India International Water Week 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, centred on the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management.” Union Minister for Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil, MoS Shri V. Somanna & Shri Raj Bhushan… pic.twitter.com/ELgtxDQVnE
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that water is the foundation of life and civilisations, stressing the need for its judicious use, conservation and effective management. Recalling his childhood experiences in Tamil Nadu, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that he had personally witnessed water scarcity and remembered the importance attached to bringing potable water to people. “Saving water is of paramount importance for humanity and the globe,” he said. The Vice-President recalled that more than two decades ago, he undertook a 19,000-km Ratha Yatra across Tamil Nadu, one of the objectives of which was to create awareness about river interlinking, water conservation and proper management of water resources. He said river interlinking could help address situations where some regions face floods while others experience drought. Emphasising India’s civilisational connect with rivers, the Vice-President said Indian communities had developed rich traditions and practices for conserving, sharing and managing water over centuries. “Our traditional wisdom provides valuable lessons for addressing today’s water challenges,” he said. The Vice-President noted that India accounts for about 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area and 18 per cent of its population, while possessing only about 4 per cent of global freshwater resources. He stressed that India’s water-use requirements cannot be compared with those of countries having greater water availability and smaller populations. Calling for behavioural change, he urged citizens to adopt simple water-saving practices in their daily lives. “We can take a bath using two buckets or twenty buckets. The choice is ours. We can close the tap while brushing our teeth. These may appear to be small things, but within these small actions lies the interest of humanity and the world,” he said. The Vice-President said climate change, rapid urbanisation and population growth were making water management increasingly complex. He stressed the need for an integrated approach encompassing river-basin management, groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and efficient irrigation.
The Vice-President highlighted the importance of cooperation among States in addressing water-sharing issues. Appreciating the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he noted that 10 inter-State MoUs have been signed for water sharing.He appreciated the efforts of the Union Government, the Ministry of Jal Shakti and participating States in promoting cooperative solutions.He particularly highlighted the Kishau Multipurpose Project agreement among six States as an important example of inter-State cooperation. Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that as India moves towards becoming a developed economy by 2047, efficient and sustainable water management will be critical. He recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call for “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari” and urged citizens to make water conservation a mass movement. He emphasised the need for greater water-use efficiency, recycling and reuse, particularly in view of the substantial demand for water from agriculture and the growing requirements of industry.He called for a shift from reactive to predictive and technology-enabled water management. Calling for a multi-stakeholder and multi-dimensional approach, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said water challenges cannot be addressed by any single institution, sector or State.He expressed confidence that the deliberations at India International Water Week-2026 would generate innovative technological, policy, socio-economic and environmental approaches for climate-resilient and integrated water management. Urging all participants to share knowledge, build partnerships and commit themselves to saving and conserving water, the Vice-President said, “Jal Suraksha will lead to Jan Suraksha and Rashtra Suraksha.” On the occasion, the Vice-President launched the Sustainable Urban River Management (SURM) Framework and AI/ML-driven Integrated Reservoir Sediment Management, marking important steps towards technology-enabled and climate-resilient water management. Union Minister of Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil, Ministers of State for Jal Shakti Shri V. Somanna and Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Secretaries of the Ministry of Jal Shakti Smt. Archana Varma and Shri Ashok Meena, Chairman, Central Water Commission, Shri Anupam Prasad, and delegates and experts from India and abroad were present on the occasion.

Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the 9th India International Water Week 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, centred on the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management.” Union Minister for Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil, MoS Shri V. Somanna & Shri Raj Bhushan… pic.twitter.com/ELgtxDQVnE
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that water is the foundation of life and civilisations, stressing the need for its judicious use, conservation and effective management. Recalling his childhood experiences in Tamil Nadu, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that he had personally witnessed water scarcity and remembered the importance attached to bringing potable water to people. “Saving water is of paramount importance for humanity and the globe,” he said. The Vice-President recalled that more than two decades ago, he undertook a 19,000-km Ratha Yatra across Tamil Nadu, one of the objectives of which was to create awareness about river interlinking, water conservation and proper management of water resources. He said river interlinking could help address situations where some regions face floods while others experience drought. Emphasising India’s civilisational connect with rivers, the Vice-President said Indian communities had developed rich traditions and practices for conserving, sharing and managing water over centuries. “Our traditional wisdom provides valuable lessons for addressing today’s water challenges,” he said. The Vice-President noted that India accounts for about 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area and 18 per cent of its population, while possessing only about 4 per cent of global freshwater resources. He stressed that India’s water-use requirements cannot be compared with those of countries having greater water availability and smaller populations. Calling for behavioural change, he urged citizens to adopt simple water-saving practices in their daily lives. “We can take a bath using two buckets or twenty buckets. The choice is ours. We can close the tap while brushing our teeth. These may appear to be small things, but within these small actions lies the interest of humanity and the world,” he said. The Vice-President said climate change, rapid urbanisation and population growth were making water management increasingly complex. He stressed the need for an integrated approach encompassing river-basin management, groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and efficient irrigation.
The Vice-President highlighted the importance of cooperation among States in addressing water-sharing issues. Appreciating the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he noted that 10 inter-State MoUs have been signed for water sharing.He appreciated the efforts of the Union Government, the Ministry of Jal Shakti and participating States in promoting cooperative solutions.He particularly highlighted the Kishau Multipurpose Project agreement among six States as an important example of inter-State cooperation. Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that as India moves towards becoming a developed economy by 2047, efficient and sustainable water management will be critical. He recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call for “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari” and urged citizens to make water conservation a mass movement. He emphasised the need for greater water-use efficiency, recycling and reuse, particularly in view of the substantial demand for water from agriculture and the growing requirements of industry.He called for a shift from reactive to predictive and technology-enabled water management. Calling for a multi-stakeholder and multi-dimensional approach, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said water challenges cannot be addressed by any single institution, sector or State.He expressed confidence that the deliberations at India International Water Week-2026 would generate innovative technological, policy, socio-economic and environmental approaches for climate-resilient and integrated water management. Urging all participants to share knowledge, build partnerships and commit themselves to saving and conserving water, the Vice-President said, “Jal Suraksha will lead to Jan Suraksha and Rashtra Suraksha.” On the occasion, the Vice-President launched the Sustainable Urban River Management (SURM) Framework and AI/ML-driven Integrated Reservoir Sediment Management, marking important steps towards technology-enabled and climate-resilient water management. Union Minister of Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil, Ministers of State for Jal Shakti Shri V. Somanna and Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Secretaries of the Ministry of Jal Shakti Smt. Archana Varma and Shri Ashok Meena, Chairman, Central Water Commission, Shri Anupam Prasad, and delegates and experts from India and abroad were present on the occasion.

title: Vice-President calls for modernising tea industry, strengthening research and building Indian tea brands for global markets
text:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the Centenary Conference of the UPASI (United Planters’ Association of Southern India) Tea Research Foundation at Coonoor, The Nilgiris, and called for greater research, modernisation, branding and value addition to make Indian tea more competitive in global markets.
Vice-President Thiru C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Centenary Conference of the UPASI (United Planters’ Association of Southern India) Tea Research Foundation at Coonoor, Nilgiris, today. The Vice President called for strengthening tea research, modernising factories, improving… pic.twitter.com/TCZHWM0HTn
He said India is among the world’s largest tea-producing and tea-consuming countries and emphasised the need to focus on both cultivation and efficient processing and manufacturing of tea.
The Vice-President called for expanding research in the tea sector, particularly in areas that can improve cost-effectiveness, quality and productivity. He also emphasised the need to educate planters on maintaining quality and responding to changing market requirements, noting that the global tea market is becoming increasingly competitive.
Referring to competition from other tea-producing countries, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said India needs to examine how its tea can be marketed more effectively, improve revenues and address the challenges faced by the plantation sector through sustained research and innovation.
He urged stakeholders to undertake a systematic assessment of the requirements of the tea industry and work with the Central and State Governments to develop concrete project proposals. He also stressed the need to identify professionals for research, modernise tea factories and undertake necessary renovation to ensure that Indian tea production meets global standards.
The Vice-President called upon tea producers and exporters to move beyond bulk tea and develop strong Indian brands.Drawing from his experience of travelling to several countries, he recalled seeing a wide range of tea brands from several countries in international markets and noted the need for greater visibility of Indian tea brands.
He suggested that stakeholders come together to market Indian tea under strong brands, which could help improve market positioning as well as revenues and prices.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan also called upon UPASI to use its centenary year to create a lasting institutional landmark by expanding the tea research network to more locations and equipping research centres with modern facilities. He said research must continuously evolve to address emerging challenges and opportunities.
Highlighting the important role of plantation workers, the Vice-President called for greater attention to their welfare.He emphasised that the welfare of plantation workers must remain an integral part of the growth and sustainability of the industry.“Industry welfare and workers’ welfare should go hand in hand,” he said.
The Vice-President stressed the importance of value addition in tea and called upon leading stakeholders to work together to identify new products, processes and market opportunities.
He pointed out that India has the advantage of being both a major tea-producing and tea-consuming country and urged the industry to make greater use of its large domestic market.The Vice-President said the present environment provides an opportunity for stakeholders to work closely with the Government to strengthen the tea sector.
The Centenary Conference brought together stakeholders from the tea and plantation sector, including planters, researchers, industry representatives and other dignitaries, to deliberate on the future of tea research and the plantation industry.
During the occasion, the Vice-President released the book “Tea Research in South India – A Compendium”, documenting the rich legacy and contributions of tea research in southern India.
Governor of Tamil Nadu, Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar; MLA, Udhagamandalam, Shri Bhojarajan; Deputy Chairman of the Tea Board of India, Shri C. Murugan; President, UPASI, Shri Ajoy Thipaiah; and other dignitaries, planters, agricultural scientists and industry representatives were present at the event.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurates 38th Pune Festival
text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the 38th Pune Festival at Shri Ganesh Kala Krida Rangmanch, Pune.
Maharashtra Governor Shri Jishnu Dev Varma, Deputy Chief Minister Smt. Sunetra Pawar, Minister for Higher & Technical Education Shri Chandrakant Patil, Minister for Cultural Affairs Shri Ashish Shelar, MP Smt. Hema Malini, MP Dr. Medha Kulkarni and former Union Home Minister Shri Sushil kumar Shinde were among those present.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the 38th Pune Festival in Pune today. The Vice President said that Pune has emerged as a major centre of education, industry, sports, information technology, automobile manufacturing, tourism and horticulture, while retaining… pic.twitter.com/FmDGHcwa3K
The Vice-President said that the nation must never forget its history and the great sacrifices made by its heroes. Recalling the enduring legacy of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, he said that his contribution to the preservation of Hindu Dharma and India’s civilisational heritage must always be remembered. He also highlighted the deep historical and cultural bonds between Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, noting that Tamil literary works have been preserved at the Saraswathi Mahal Library in Thanjavur because of Maratha leaders .
He also paid tribute to Lokmanya Tilak, Mahatma Jyotiba Phule, Krantijyoti Savitribai Phule and Babasaheb B. R. Ambedkar.
Appreciating Pune’s growing global character, the Vice-President particularly lauded the performance of international students at the inauguration session. He noted that students from around 20 countries participated in Traditional Ganesh Worship programme , describing it as a beautiful manifestation of the spirit of “Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.”
The Vice-President said Pune has emerged as a major centre of education, industry, sports, information technology, automobile manufacturing, tourism and horticulture, while retaining its cultural identity. He credited the Pune Festival with contributing significantly to Pune’s emergence as a “City of Festivals” and appreciated the vision of its founder, late Shri Suresh Kalmadi.
Appreciating the festival’s focus on young and emerging artists, the Vice-President highlighted programmes such as Ugavate Tare and Indradhanu. He also commended the Mahila Mahotsav for providing women artists a platform to showcase their talent and creativity.
Emphasising the need to remain rooted in India’s civilisational heritage, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that development must go hand in hand with preservation of heritage. Referring to the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi,” he said modernity and technological advancement need not come at the cost of traditions and cultural values.
The Vice-President said the vision of Viksit Bharat encompasses not only economic growth and infrastructure but also an inclusive and equitable society rooted in its civilisational heritage. He noted that festivals such as the Pune Festival can promote cultural exchange, tourism, local talent and national integration.
Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan prayed to Lord Ganesha for continued unity, harmony and service, and expressed the hope that the Pune Festival would continue to celebrate India’s composite culture, inspire young talent, empower women, promote tourism and strengthen national integration.
The Vice-President also presented the Founder Suresh Kalmadi Pune Festival Lifetime Achievement Award to veteran actor Shri Mohan Joshi, recognising his distinguished contribution to Indian cinema and the performing arts.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Addresses Platinum Jubilee Celebrations of Gordhandas Seksaria College of Yoga and Cultural Synthesis
text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of the Gordhandas Seksaria College of Yoga and Cultural Synthesis at Kaivalyadhama, Lonavala, Maharashtra.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of Gordhandas Seksaria College of Yoga and Cultural Synthesis at Kaivalyadhama, Lonavala. Congratulating the College on completing 75 years of dedicated service to Yoga education, research and… pic.twitter.com/HuBp777tEu
He congratulated the College on completing 75 years of dedicated service to Yoga education, research and cultural synthesis. He noted that the occasion was especially significant as Kaivalyadhama itself has completed a century of dedicated service to Yoga.
Recalling the contribution of Swami Kuvalayananda, who founded Kaivalyadhama in 1924, the Vice-President said that he pioneered the scientific study of Yoga at a time when it was largely viewed as a mystical practice. He emphasised that the legacies of the past must be preserved and carried forward for future generations. “Yoga is not for one generation; it is for every generation to come,” he said.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan highlighted the growing global acceptance of Yoga and recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s sustained efforts in taking its message to the international stage. He noted that Yoga is today practised across nations, cultures and communities.
Observing that technological progress and digital connectivity have made life increasingly fast-paced, the Vice-President said Yoga provides an opportunity to pause, concentrate, reflect and reconnect with oneself. He said Yoga helps bridge the gap between mind and body and promotes physical and mental well-being.
Addressing the young students, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said India’s youth possess immense energy, talent and ambition, which achieve their fullest potential when combined with discipline and awareness. Referring to Patanjali’s concept of chitta vritti nirodhah, he said the ability to calm and focus the mind is particularly relevant in an age of constant notifications and information overload.
The Vice-President said that any endeavour undertaken with good intention and with a sincere commitment to the well-being of society can leave a lasting legacy. Good legacies never die; they continue to inspire and benefit generations to come. The century-long journey of Kaivalyadhama is a living testament to this enduring truth.
The Vice-President congratulated the Trustees, Principal, faculty, students and alumni of the College and paid tribute to the vision of Swami Kuvalayananda and the contribution of Seth Makhanlal Seksaria.
On the occasion, the Vice-President also launched “Yoga Explained – Learn From the Master” by Shri O. P. Tiwari. He visited the campus and interacted with the students, encouraging them to cultivate the values of discipline, concentration and self-awareness through the practice of Yoga.
Governor of Maharashtra Shri Jishnu Dev Varma, former Union Minister and Chairman of Kaivalyadhama Global Shri Suresh Prabhu, CEO of Kaivalyadhama Global Shri Subodh Tiwari, Chief Patron Shri Rakesh Seksaria, faculty members, students, alumni and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan participates in Hyderabad Liberation Day celebrations in Telangana
text:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today participated as the Chief Guest at the 79th Hyderabad Liberation Day celebrations held at Parade Ground, Secunderabad, Telangana.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan participated as Chief Guest at the 79th Hyderabad Liberation Day celebrations at Parade Ground, Secunderabad, Telangana today. 

He described Hyderabad Liberation as a decisive chapter in the history of independent Bharat and paid homage to the countless patriots who displayed courage and made immense sacrifices in the struggle for liberation and integration.
Addressing the gathering, the Vice President said that 17 September 1948 marked the conclusion of a decisive chapter in the history of independent Bharat, with the integration of the erstwhile Hyderabad State into the Indian Union following the events of September 1948 and Operation Polo.He said that Hyderabad Liberation Day is not merely a commemoration of a historic date, but a reminder of the journey of nation-building and the values that continue to bind Bharat together. He said the story of Hyderabad reflects the enormous challenges faced by a young nation in bringing together people who had emerged from different political circumstances. It was a story of statesmanship, courage and sacrifice, followed by the larger and continuing task of building a constitutional democracy in which every citizen has an equal place. Recalling Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s contribution to national integration, the Vice-President said that as the first Home Minister and Minister for States, Sardar Patel carried an extraordinary responsibility at a time when India was recovering from Partition and simultaneously consolidating hundreds of princely states into one Union. “Sardar Patel Ji laid the steely foundation of a strong, unified Ek Bharat,” Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said. Drawing a parallel between different phases of India’s nation-building, the Vice-President said: “Gandhi Ji and Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Ji played a pivotal role in India’s freedom. Sardar Patel Ji played a pivotal role in unifying princely states with modern-day India. Prime Minister Narendra Modi Ji is now playing a pivotal role in the making of developed India -Viksit Bharat @ 2047.” Paying tribute to the people’s movement behind the Hyderabad struggle, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that students, intellectuals, writers, social workers, political activists, farmers and ordinary citizens participated in the struggle and endured imprisonment, violence and immense personal hardship. He paid homage to patriots including Ramji Gond, Turrebaz Khan and Komaram Bheem, among many others, and said their courage reminds us that history is not made only in government offices or by famous statesmen, but also by ordinary citizens who refuse to accept injustice as their destiny. “Political integration can bring territories together; constitutional democracy brings citizens together,” he said, stressing that national unity cannot be sustained by geography alone and must be strengthened through equal rights, equal dignity and equal opportunity. He said Bharat’s unity does not require every citizen to be identical, noting that Indians may speak different languages, follow different traditions, worship differently and hold different political opinions, yet remain bound together by the Constitution and the principle that sovereignty ultimately belongs to the people. Referring to the role of the Central Armed Police Forces, the Vice-President said that they had played an important role in the integration of princely states and in safeguarding the territorial integrity of Bharat in 1947–48. He also acknowledged their contribution in combating Left-Wing Extremism in Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and other affected areas.
The Vice-President visited the War Memorial and laid a wreath, paying tributes to the bravehearts.
He also inspected the parade and witnessed the impressive March Past and evocative cultural performances at the event. He said the legacy of Hyderabad must remind the nation that integration must lead to inclusion, and patriotism must ultimately find its highest expression in service to the nation.

Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today participated as the Chief Guest at the 79th Hyderabad Liberation Day celebrations held at Parade Ground, Secunderabad, Telangana.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan participated as Chief Guest at the 79th Hyderabad Liberation Day celebrations at Parade Ground, Secunderabad, Telangana today. 

He described Hyderabad Liberation as a decisive chapter in the history of independent Bharat and paid homage to the countless patriots who displayed courage and made immense sacrifices in the struggle for liberation and integration.
Addressing the gathering, the Vice President said that 17 September 1948 marked the conclusion of a decisive chapter in the history of independent Bharat, with the integration of the erstwhile Hyderabad State into the Indian Union following the events of September 1948 and Operation Polo.He said that Hyderabad Liberation Day is not merely a commemoration of a historic date, but a reminder of the journey of nation-building and the values that continue to bind Bharat together. He said the story of Hyderabad reflects the enormous challenges faced by a young nation in bringing together people who had emerged from different political circumstances. It was a story of statesmanship, courage and sacrifice, followed by the larger and continuing task of building a constitutional democracy in which every citizen has an equal place. Recalling Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s contribution to national integration, the Vice-President said that as the first Home Minister and Minister for States, Sardar Patel carried an extraordinary responsibility at a time when India was recovering from Partition and simultaneously consolidating hundreds of princely states into one Union. “Sardar Patel Ji laid the steely foundation of a strong, unified Ek Bharat,” Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said. Drawing a parallel between different phases of India’s nation-building, the Vice-President said: “Gandhi Ji and Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Ji played a pivotal role in India’s freedom. Sardar Patel Ji played a pivotal role in unifying princely states with modern-day India. Prime Minister Narendra Modi Ji is now playing a pivotal role in the making of developed India -Viksit Bharat @ 2047.” Paying tribute to the people’s movement behind the Hyderabad struggle, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that students, intellectuals, writers, social workers, political activists, farmers and ordinary citizens participated in the struggle and endured imprisonment, violence and immense personal hardship. He paid homage to patriots including Ramji Gond, Turrebaz Khan and Komaram Bheem, among many others, and said their courage reminds us that history is not made only in government offices or by famous statesmen, but also by ordinary citizens who refuse to accept injustice as their destiny. “Political integration can bring territories together; constitutional democracy brings citizens together,” he said, stressing that national unity cannot be sustained by geography alone and must be strengthened through equal rights, equal dignity and equal opportunity. He said Bharat’s unity does not require every citizen to be identical, noting that Indians may speak different languages, follow different traditions, worship differently and hold different political opinions, yet remain bound together by the Constitution and the principle that sovereignty ultimately belongs to the people. Referring to the role of the Central Armed Police Forces, the Vice-President said that they had played an important role in the integration of princely states and in safeguarding the territorial integrity of Bharat in 1947–48. He also acknowledged their contribution in combating Left-Wing Extremism in Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and other affected areas.
The Vice-President visited the War Memorial and laid a wreath, paying tributes to the bravehearts.
He also inspected the parade and witnessed the impressive March Past and evocative cultural performances at the event. He said the legacy of Hyderabad must remind the nation that integration must lead to inclusion, and patriotism must ultimately find its highest expression in service to the nation.

title: Vice-President hails DNHDD as a “Mini India”, appreciates transformative development under PM Narendra Modi and Administrator Praful Patel
text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed a public function at Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Government College, Silvassa, during his maiden visit to the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed a public function at Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Government College, Silvassa today, during his maiden visit to the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

The Vice-President said that the Union Territory is a remarkable example of how innovative governance and people’s participation can drive transformative development.

The Vice-President appreciated the Union Territory’s social diversity, cultural heritage and spirit of harmony and described it as a “mini India”. He said that people from different parts of the country are contributing to the region’s growth and living together in harmony.
On the occasion, the Vice-President was felicitated by public representatives, including Hon’ble Administrator Shri Praful Patel and Hon’ble Member of Parliament Smt. Kalaben Mohanbhai Delkar, along with representatives of District Panchayats, Municipal Councils, industry and hotel associations, topper students from various colleges and the Tamil Sangam. He also distributed toolkits to PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries and appointment certificates to newly appointed teachers.
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that the Union Territory is a remarkable example of how innovative governance and people’s participation can drive transformative development. He appreciated the progress achieved over the last decade under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the sustained efforts of Administrator Shri Praful Patel, with active participation of the people.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that over 450 infrastructure projects worth more than ₹13,000 crore have been undertaken in the Union Territory during the last decade, including around 800 km of roads at a cost of over ₹4,000 crore.
Highlighting the transformation in healthcare, he noted that the Union Territory, which did not have a medical college before 2019, now has one with 177 seats, besides the 450-bed NAMO Hospital in Silvassa and the recently inaugurated 350-bed NAMO Hospital in Daman. TB cases have declined by 57 per cent and malnutrition by 58 per cent over the last three years. The Union Territory has also achieved 100 per cent saturation of Health and Wellness Centres and institutional deliveries, along with full registration under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission.
On education, the Vice-President highlighted the construction of 21 new schools at an investment of over ₹700 crore, with 16 more under construction, besides smart classrooms in government schools. He also noted the establishment of institutions and campuses of NIFT, Gujarat National Law University and other professional institutions, expanding opportunities for the youth within the Union Territory.
Highlighting the growing importance of tourism, the Vice-President noted that tourist footfall has increased from around 6 lakh in 2021 to nearly 50 lakh in 2025. He said that initiatives such as the Daman Night Market, Ram-setu Seafront, restored heritage sites, beaches, water sports and eco-tourism projects are creating new opportunities while showcasing the region’s rich heritage and natural beauty.
The Vice-President also highlighted the Union Territory’s industrial strength, with more than 7,500 manufacturing units and over 2.8 lakh employment opportunities through the MSME sector. The inauguration of Namo Airport, Daman has further strengthened air connectivity with Delhi, Mumbai and Ahmedabad. He also appreciated the Union Territory for achieving 100 per cent solarisation of government buildings, with nearly 12 MW of installed capacity.
Referring to the contributions of Gujarat’s three iconic leaders, Mahatma Gandhi, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President said that Gandhi represents non-violence and the freedom struggle, Sardar Patel symbolises the unity and integrity of India, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi represents development.
The Vice-President said that the Union Territory’s social diversity, cultural heritage and spirit of harmony make it a “mini India”. He said that people from different parts of the country are contributing to the region’s growth and living together in harmony.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan visits Donyi-Polo Mission School for Specially Abled Children in Itanagar
text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today visited the Donyi-Polo Mission School for the Hearing, Visually and Intellectually Impaired at Chimpu, Itanagar, and interacted with students, teachers and staff. He visited various activity areas of the institution and addressed the students.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan visited the Donyi-Polo Mission School for the Hearing, Visually and Intellectually Impaired at Chimpu, Itanagar today, and interacted with students, teachers and staff. Speaking on the occasion, the Vice-President said that his visit to… pic.twitter.com/yUdvh7y7PH
Speaking on the occasion, the Vice-President said that his visit to the institution filled him with a deep sense of emotion and patriotism, particularly after listening to the students sing Vande Mataram. He said the song was rendered with such sincerity that he could feel the patriotism “coming from the heart” of the students. Appreciating the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the Donyi-Polo Mission, the management, teachers, rehabilitation professionals and staff, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the achievements of the State Government under Chief Minister Shri Pema Khandu cover “every spectrum of society”. Addressing the students, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan urged them never to allow anyone to define the limits of their dreams. “Every individual is unique. Every individual possesses talent,” he said, encouraging them to dream big, believe in themselves and work hard. Referring to the inspiring journey of Shri Srikanth Bolla, he urged the students to draw inspiration from those who have overcome challenges. The Vice-President said that institutions such as the Donyi-Polo Mission School provide not merely education but also hope, dignity, opportunity, confidence and self-reliance. He said such institutions make a meaningful contribution towards building an inclusive Viksit Bharat @ 2047. Emphasising the transformative potential of technology, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that Artificial Intelligence, digital tools and assistive technologies can help overcome barriers and make education more accessible and personalised. He appreciated the Mission’s initiatives towards AI-enabled learning materials and holistic support for students. The Vice-President also commended the teachers and staff for their extraordinary patience, compassion and commitment in nurturing children with special needs. He acknowledged the important role played by parents in supporting and encouraging their children. Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said, “Today, you have taught me a lot of things,” conveying his appreciation for the inspiration he drew from the students and their determination. The Vice-President was accompanied by Governor of Arunachal Pradesh Lt. General (Retd.) Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik, Chief Minister Shri Pema Khandu, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein, Minister for Social Justice & Empowerment and Tribal Affairs Shri Konto Jini, senior officials of the State Government, representatives of the Donyi-Polo Mission and its management, teachers, rehabilitation professionals, staff and students of the institution. Earlier today, the Vice-President also visited the J. N. State Museum in Itanagar and appreciated its role in preserving and showcasing the rich ethnographic heritage of Arunachal Pradesh and the North-East. He noted that such institutions serve as vital bridges between generations and play an important role in safeguarding cultural heritage and fostering pride in indigenous traditions. He commended the dedicated efforts of all those associated with the Museum in preserving and promoting the invaluable heritage of Arunachal Pradesh.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, visited the J. N. State Museum in Itanagar, which preserves and showcases the rich ethnographic heritage of Arunachal Pradesh and the North-East. title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan visits Nyedar Namlo in Itanagar; highlights need to preserve indigenous faith, culture and knowledge systems
text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today visited Nyedar Namlo in Itanagar, a sacred place of worship and community hub associated with the indigenous Donyi-Polo faith of the Nyishi community and other indigenous groups of Arunachal Pradesh.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan visited Nyedar Namlo in Itanagar today, a sacred place of worship and community hub associated with the indigenous Donyi-Polo faith of the Nyishi community and other indigenous groups of Arunachal Pradesh. The Vice-President offered… pic.twitter.com/iRHxfwgqoD
The Vice-President offered prayers at the prayer hall and was briefed on the Nyishi indigenous faith, beliefs and prayer systems, the Yerko indigenous Gurukul system, preservation of traditional knowledge and medicinal practices, and efforts to promote the mother tongue.
Addressing a community gathering, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said he felt blessed to visit Nyedar Namlo during his first visit to Arunachal Pradesh. He said he was honoured to be at a place “where traditions become modern thinking, and modern thinking is not destroying traditions.”
He described Arunachal Pradesh as a proud embodiment of India’s unity in diversity, where ancient traditions and modern aspirations walk together. He also said that the people of Arunachal Pradesh stand as proud sentinels of India’s territorial integrity.
Highlighting the values of the Donyi-Polo tradition, the Vice-President said its emphasis on nature, truth, harmony and community remains deeply relevant to the modern world. He stressed that development must go hand in hand with cultural preservation.
Appreciating the efforts of the Nyishi Nyidung Mung-jwng Rallung, he said its work in documentation, research, traditional festivals, cultural activities and preservation of customary laws and social values is making an important contribution to the community’s cultural future.
He also highlighted the Yerko Gurukul system, saying it offers an important model of combining contemporary education with indigenous knowledge, enabling children to embrace modern opportunities while remaining connected to their roots.
Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi”, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said tribal communities are not merely custodians of India’s past but important partners in building its future. He noted that the recognition of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas has brought renewed national attention to the invaluable contributions of India’s tribal communities. He also linked preservation of indigenous traditions with the spirit of Vocal for Local and Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat.
“Preservation of indigenous culture is not about resisting change. It is about ensuring that change does not come at the cost of identity,” he said.
Calling upon the youth to embrace modern science, technology and global skills while remaining connected to their mother tongue and traditions, the Vice-President said India must be modern in its aspirations but deeply rooted in its civilisational and cultural values.
He extended his best wishes to the Nyedar Namlo movement and expressed hope that the sacred place would continue to inspire peace, harmony, respect for nature, social unity and a strong sense of community.
Among those present on the occasion were Governor of Arunachal Pradesh Lt. Gen. (Retd.) Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik, Chief Minister Shri Pema Khandu, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein, Member of Parliament Shri Tai Tagak, Minister for Home and Indigenous Affairs Shri Mama Natung and Chief Secretary Shri Manish Kumar Gupta.

title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan addresses Special Session of Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly
text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the Special Session of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly in Itanagar, calling upon legislators to uphold the highest traditions of democracy and work towards the development of the State and the nation.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Special Session of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly in Itanagar today, and called upon the legislators to uphold the highest traditions of democracy and work towards the development of the State and the nation. The… pic.twitter.com/DqaslGe58V
On his arrival at the Assembly premises, the Vice-President paid floral tributes to the statues of Mahatma Gandhi and Babasaheb Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and was accorded a ceremonial Guard of Honour. He also visited the Arunachal Pradesh Assembly Museum, which showcases the evolution and growth of the State Legislature and its legislative journey. Addressing the Assembly, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that Arunachal Pradesh has immense strategic importance, rich cultural heritage and abundant natural resources, and plays a vital role in safeguarding the nation’s borders. He noted that the security of the rest of the country is closely linked to the protection of the borders by the people of Arunachal Pradesh. Emphasising India’s unity amid its diversity, the Vice-President said that the country is united by one Constitution, one vision of ‘Rashtra Pratham’ (Nation First) and one goal of Viksit Bharat @ 2047. Quoting national poet Subramania Bharati, he highlighted the unity of thought underlying India’s diverse languages and traditions. Recalling India’s rich democratic heritage, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan described India as the ‘Mother of Democracy’ and urged legislators to live up to this legacy. The Vice-President highlighted the growing focus on the development of the North-East, recalling the establishment of the Ministry of DoNER during the tenure of former Prime Minister Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee and the emphasis on the region under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Act East Policy. He congratulated the Government and people of Arunachal Pradesh for the State’s development achievements, including its emergence as the country’s leading producer of kiwi, expansion of road infrastructure, issuance of over one lakh Soil Health Cards and significant progress in education and per capita income. Congratulating the State Legislature on completing its Golden Jubilee, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated initiatives such as making the Legislative Secretariat plastic-free and establishing the Assembly Library and Museum. Urging legislators to place public service above electoral success, the Vice-President said that elections may be won through votes, but the respect and trust of people can only be earned through dedicated service. He called upon Members to make effective use of Question Hour and Zero Hour to raise issues concerning public policy and their constituencies. As the Presiding Officer of the Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasised the importance of dialogue, debate and discussion in legislative functioning. Reiterating his message that “debates, discussions, or even disruptions must always lead to a decision,” he said that healthy debate strengthens democracy and constructive cooperation advances the State and the nation. The Vice-President said that there can be no Viksit Bharat without a Viksit Arunachal Pradesh, stressing that development must be inclusive and no tribal or marginalised community should be left behind. He also emphasised the need to balance environmental concerns with responsible utilisation of natural resources for the economic development and welfare of the people. Referring to Arunachal Pradesh’s significant hydropower potential, he said its appropriate utilisation could generate greater revenue and accelerate the State’s development. Governor of Arunachal Pradesh Lt. Gen. (Retd.) Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik, Speaker of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly Shri Tesam Pongte, Chief Minister Shri Pema Khandu, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein, Members of the Legislative Assembly, senior officials of the State Government and Legislative Secretariat were present on the occasion.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan visits INA Museum at Moirang and Sainik School Imphal
text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today visited the INA Museum at Moirang, Manipur paying homage to the valour and sacrifice of the Indian National Army (INA). He visited the historic site where the Indian Tricolour was first hoisted on the Indian mainland by the INA and toured the INA War Museum gallery. He also paid floral tribute to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, visited the INA Museum at Moirang, Manipur, today. He visited the historic site where the Tricolour was first hoisted on Indian soil by the Indian National Army, and toured the INA War Museum gallery, commemorating the valour and… pic.twitter.com/rCImPj8ijr
Later, the Vice-President visited Sainik School Imphal, where he paid floral tribute at the War Memorial and was accorded a Guard of Honour by the cadets.
The Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan visited Sainik School Imphal, where he paid floral tribute at the War Memorial and was accorded a Guard of Honour by the cadets. He joined the cadets for lunch at the Mess and subsequently addressed and interacted with them. Addressing… pic.twitter.com/aslscwHTpM
Speaking on his visit to Moirang at the School, the Vice-President recalled the historic role of the INA in India’s freedom struggle. He noted that several freedom fighters from across the country, including many from Tamil Nadu, had joined the INA and made the supreme sacrifice for the nation. He also recalled his recent visit to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose had hoisted the Indian Tricolour, and said that these historic sites remind the younger generation of the courage, patriotism and sacrifices of India’s freedom fighters. The Vice-President emphasised that the true legacy of an institution is reflected not merely in its buildings or records, but in the character of its students and alumni. He called upon the cadets to particularly develop discipline, courage and leadership. “Even if you are less talented, with discipline you will shine,” Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said, stressing that discipline provides the foundation for excellence. On courage, he said that true courage also means standing up for others when someone is being unnecessarily harmed. On leadership, he emphasised that a true leader accepts responsibility, sets an example, listens to others and has the moral courage to take the right decision. Highlighting the importance of national integration, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that India’s diversity of languages, traditions and regions is united by a shared national identity. He said Sainik Schools have a special role in strengthening the spirit of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat, as students from diverse backgrounds learn, train, eat and play together. Referring to the rapid pace of technological change, he urged the cadets to preserve the timeless values of discipline, integrity and patriotism while also becoming adaptable, innovative and technologically aware. He mentioned emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, space technology, biotechnology, cybersecurity and robotics as areas offering new opportunities to the younger generation. During his interaction with the cadets, the Vice-President described the Northeast as an integral and beautiful part of India and praised the hard work and contribution of its people. He encouraged the students to retain their goodness while adapting themselves to change, observing that change is the only constant in the world. Responding to a question on his visit to Cellular Jail in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan encouraged the students to visit the historic site to understand the hardships endured by India’s freedom fighters. He said such a visit inspires patriotism and reminds the younger generation of the sacrifices made during the freedom struggle. On the role of students in building a developed India, the Vice-President said that every student can contribute by performing their duty to the best of their ability every day. He emphasised that doing one’s best each day would collectively contribute to the realisation of Viksit Bharat. The Vice-President was accompanied by Governor of Manipur Shri Ajay Kumar Bhalla, Chief Minister Shri Y. Khemchand Singh, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Defence Smt. Deepti Mohil Chawla, Major General Shubhankar Basu, VSM, Inspecting Officer, Sainik Schools Society, Ministry of Defence, Brigadier Amit Chatterjee, and Principal, Sainik School Imphal, Colonel A. Rajiv, among other dignitaries.

title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan attends public reception in Shillong; lays foundation stones for projects worth over ₹1,000 crore
text:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today attended a public reception organised in his honour by the people and Government of Meghalaya at Soso Tham Auditorium, Shillong. He expressed gratitude for the warm welcome and said he would always stand with the people of Meghalaya in the State’s development journey.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced a public reception organised in his honour by the people and Government of Meghalaya at Soso Tham Auditorium, Shillong today. The Vice President laid the foundation stones for five projects worth over ₹1000 crores. These include… pic.twitter.com/OZqJPC1g2Y
The Vice-President highlighted Meghalaya’s rich cultural heritage, natural beauty and unique social institutions, including its matrilineal heritage. He said the State’s vibrant grassroots institutions reflect India’s diversity and democratic traditions. Recalling his former Lok Sabha colleague, late Shri P. A. Sangma, he described him as a great leader and an outstanding speaker who made a significant contribution to parliamentary democracy. Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said true secularism means respecting each other’s thoughts an beliefs. He emphasised that people must live together with mutual respect and harmony. He also stressed that development must be inclusive and no section of society should be left behind. Highlighting the importance of connectivity, the Vice-President said every effort is being made to connect remote villages with towns and cities. He noted that over 46,000 km of rural roads have been constructed in the North-East under PMGSY in the last decade, with expenditure of over ₹47,000 crore. He also appreciated Meghalaya’s reform-linked MoU under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. The Vice President laid the foundation stones for five projects worth ₹1,010.95 crore. These include the New Shillong Water Supply Scheme Phase II, Part A (₹850.58 crore) under the Urban Challenge Fund, two road connectivity projects under NESIDS, a 30-bedded AYUSH facility at Shillong Civil Hospital and a 132/33 KV substation at Mawkhanu under PM-DevINE. He also inaugurated the Maternity and Children’s Hospital at Nongstoin, completed at a cost of ₹31.05 crore under the National Health Mission. He said the projects, together worth about ₹1,042 crore, will strengthen water supply, connectivity, healthcare and power infrastructure in Meghalaya. The Vice-President appreciated the State Government’s initiatives in infrastructure and tourism, including the homestay programme, CM-Elevate and Green Meghalaya. He congratulated Chief Minister Shri Conrad K. Sangma, his Council of Ministers and the people of Meghalaya for the State’s progress. Speaking on the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasised that progress must be inclusive, leaving no section of society behind, while preserving Meghalaya’s rich environment, culture and traditions. Referring to the State’s living-root bridges and the landscapes of Sohra and Mawsynram, he said Meghalaya offers valuable lessons in living in harmony with nature. Chief Minister Shri Conrad K. Sangma, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Prestone Tynsong and Shri Sniawbhalang Dhar, Minister Shri Sanbor Shullai, Chief Secretary Dr. Shakil P. Ahammed and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

title: Vice-President lays foundation stone for ₹110 crore infrastructure projects at Gauhati University
text:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today laid the foundation stone for ₹110 crore infrastructure development projects at Gauhati University, including a new multidisciplinary academic building, a new boys’ and international students’ hostel, and works related to the auditorium and library.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan laid the foundation stone for ₹110 crore infrastructure development projects at Gauhati University today. The Vice President welcomed the translation of Assamese and Tamil literary works into each other and encouraged greater academic… pic.twitter.com/2DpbpgiZeW
Addressing the gathering, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan highlighted the historic significance of Gauhati University, established on January 26, 1948, as the first university in Northeast India, following a sustained public movement led by eminent leaders including Bharat Ratna Gopinath Bordoloi. He noted that the University has grown into a premier institution in the region, with NAAC A+ accreditation and 9th rank among State Public Universities in NIRF 2025. Appreciating the University’s efforts to preserve India’s linguistic heritage, he said language carries the memory, wisdom and identity of a civilisation. He welcomed the translation of Assamese and Tamil literary works into each other and encouraged greater academic and literary exchanges between Assam and Tamil Nadu, observing that India’s linguistic diversity is enriched by its cultural unity. Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated the University’s research on the Brahmaputra Basin, endangered languages, multilingualism, women’s studies, environmental sustainability and Indian Knowledge Systems. Describing the Brahmaputra as an ecological, economic and civilisational force, he stressed the importance of research addressing both regional and national challenges. Highlighting the expansion of India’s higher education ecosystem since 2014, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan lauded the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in expanding educational opportunities across the country, noting the establishment of new IITs, IIMs, IIITs, Central Universities, AIIMS and other institutions. He also highlighted the 42.2 per cent rise in women’s enrolment in higher education, from 1.57 crore in 2014-15 to 2.24 crore in 2023-24, describing women’s increasing participation and academic achievements as a significant indicator of empowerment. He appreciated Assam’s development trajectory under the leadership of Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma, particularly in infrastructure, connectivity, education, investment and employment. He highlighted the State’s improved education performance, the commencement of the first MBA batch at IIM Guwahati and more than 1.64 lakh merit-based government appointments since 2021. Calling upon students and scholars to contribute to Viksit Bharat @2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan urged them to dream boldly, pursue research addressing community challenges, ensure technology serves humanity and make innovation a vehicle for inclusive development. Quoting Swami Vivekananda, he urged the youth to “Awake, arise and stop not till your goal is reached.” On the occasion, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan released Bhupen Hazarika: Hundred Years of a Wandering Songs, edited by Ankuran Dutta and Nani Gopal Mahanta, and the 5th revised and enlarged edition of Chandrakanta Abhidhan. The Vice-President also witnessed a cultural programme presented by Gauhati University students, showcasing Assam’s rich cultural heritage. He also led students and other participants in taking the “No to Drugs” pledge, urging young people to stay away from substance abuse, exercise self-discipline, manage their time wisely and limit excessive social media use. The programme was attended by Governor of Assam Shri Lakshman Prasad Acharya, Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma, Education Minister Dr. Ranoj Pegu, Chief Secretary Dr. Ravi Kota, Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University Shri Nani Gopal Mahanta, Registrar Prof. Utpal Sarma, faculty members, students and other dignitaries.

title: Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attends SSUHS Convocation in Guwahati
text:
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today urged graduating healthcare professionals to uphold compassion, ethics and scientific excellence, and dedicate their knowledge and skills to the service of humanity, while addressing the convocation ceremony of Srimanta Sankaradeva University of Health Sciences (SSUHS), Guwahati. He also presented the Dr. John Berry White Award for the years 2023, 2024 and 2025.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the convocation ceremony of Srimanta Sankaradeva University of Health Sciences (SSUHS), Guwahati today. The Vice President said that the University, named after Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankaradeva, has emerged as an important… pic.twitter.com/zBsda6uZK4
Addressing the convocation, he said that the University, named after Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankaradeva, has emerged as an important institution for health sciences education, research and public health. He appreciated its efforts to promote medical knowledge in local languages, including the publication of an Anglo-Assamese Dictionary of Medical Science and medical textbooks in Assamese.
The Vice President highlighted the transformation of India’s healthcare sector under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, referring to initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat. He noted that more than 44 crore Ayushman cards have been issued and recalled that the scheme has helped poor and middle-class families save an estimated Rs. 2 lakh crore in medical expenses.
Highlighting Assam’s healthcare progress, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the number of medical colleges in the State has more than doubled from seven in 2021 to 15, with another nine under construction. He also highlighted AIIMS Guwahati, the first AIIMS in the Northeast, and Assam’s three-tier cancer-care network, including the State’s first Proton Beam Therapy Centre.
The Vice President congratulated Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma and the Government of Assam for strengthening healthcare infrastructure and said that the changing healthcare landscape is enabling patients from outside Assam to increasingly seek advanced treatment in Guwahati.
Calling upon youth to lead healthy and disciplined lives, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan urged them to stay away from substance abuse and contribute towards building a Nasha Mukt Bharat. He also advised students to use social media constructively and not allow it to consume excessive time.
The Vice President said that young healthcare professionals have a crucial role in advancing the vision of a Viksit and Swasth Bharat, and wished the graduating students success in their future endeavours.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attends Golden Jubilee celebrations of Geetanagar College in Guwahati
text:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today attended the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Geetanagar College, formerly known as Kanya Mahavidyalaya, in Guwahati. He also inaugurated the college’s new academic building.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Geetanagar College, formerly known as Kanya Mahavidyalaya, in Guwahati today. He also inaugurated the college’s new academic building during the occasion. The Vice-President described Assam as a… pic.twitter.com/un25Ju5Gvd
Congratulating the institution on completing five decades of dedicated service to higher education, Shri Radhakrishnan said that Geetanagar College has made a significant contribution to the educational and social development of Assam, particularly in empowering generations of young women through education, knowledge and confidence. Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President described Assam as a land of rich cultural heritage and traditions. He highlighted the State’s distinctive contribution to India’s cultural landscape through its languages, literature, music, dance, theatre and indigenous traditions. He also recalled the valour and patriotism of Lachit Barphukan, who remains an enduring source of inspiration for the nation. The Vice-President highlighted the emphasis placed by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on the growth and development of the North-East. He noted that Assam, with its rich natural resources, forests and globally renowned tea, has immense potential and is witnessing a remarkable phase of development. Emphasising the transformative role of education, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that institutions of higher learning must not merely prepare students for careers but also nurture responsible citizens committed to democracy, constitutional values, social responsibility and nation-building. The Vice-President led the students and those present in taking a ‘No to Drugs’ pledge, urging young people to stay away from drugs and to encourage their friends to do the same. He emphasised that students must make responsible choices and safeguard their time, health and future. He said that India’s young population is its greatest strength and that the opportunities emerging in areas such as artificial intelligence, digital technology, biotechnology, space research and entrepreneurship can enable the youth to play a leading role in building a developed India. The Vice-President appreciated the progress and transformation witnessed by Assam under the leadership of Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma. He noted that Assam has emerged as one of the fastest-growing State economies in recent years, with its economy expanding significantly. He highlighted the major investments being made in healthcare, education, infrastructure, employment and disaster management, along with the development of tea-garden communities. Also present on the occasion were Governor of Assam Shri Lakshman Prasad Acharya, Chief Minister of Assam Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma, Education Minister of Assam Dr. Ranoj Pegu, Chief Secretary of Assam Dr. Ravi Kota, Commissioner & Secretary, Higher Education Department, Shri Narayan Konwar, Principal of Geetanagar College Dr. Satyajit Kalita, and other dignitaries. Earlier, the Vice-President was received at Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, by Shri Lakshman Prasad Acharya, Hon’ble Governor of Assam; Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Assam; and other dignitaries.

During his visit to Assam, he will also attend the Convocation Ceremony of Srimanta Sankaradeva University of Health Sciences (SSUHS), Guwahati, and programmes at Gauhati University.
