title: Vice President releases commemorative postage stamp marking 75 years of Dinamalar in Chennai
text:
The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today said that Dinamalar has earned the trust of the people over the past 75 years by upholding the values of truth, patriotism and public service, and called upon the newspaper to continue serving the nation for many more years.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan released a commemorative postage stamp marking the 75th year of Dinamalar in Chennai today. He lauded Dinamalar’s 7-decade-long journey of upholding truth, patriotism and public service. pic.twitter.com/up4o6RTNKK
Addressing the function held in Chennai to mark the 75th year of publication of Dinamalar and the release of a commemorative postage stamp, the Vice President noted that Dinamalar, founded in 1951 with the resolve to serve as a touchstone of truth and Recalled the contribution of Dinamalar founder Shri T. V. Ramasubbaiyer. He observed that an idea that originated in the mind of one individual has today grown into a large organisation, reflecting the dedication and collective efforts of successive generations. Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan emphasised that a newspaper can earn and retain the trust of the people only when it stands firm against pressures and continues to uphold higher values such as patriotism and public service without fear.He said that Dinamalar’s work over the past 75 years has established such a bond of trust with its readers. The Vice President stressed the importance of nurturing the next generation and appreciated Dinamalar’s efforts through its ‘Pattam’ publication, which brings knowledge on general awareness, language skills and scientific innovations to school students. The Vice President wished Dinamalar continued growth and success, saying that it should remain a touchstone of truth, serving the nation and society for many more decades. The function was attended by Chennai Regional Director of the Department of Posts, Major Manoj; Editor of the Dinamalar Group, Dr. R. Ramasubbu; publishers Shri L. Aadhimoolam, Dr. L. Ramasubbu and Smt. Jayashree; Shri R. R. Gopalji, and other distinguished guests.

title: VICE PRESIDENT LAUNCHES INDIA VALVE REGISTRY AT INDIA VALVES 2026 IN CHENNAI
text:
The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today launched the India Valve Registry at India Valves 2026, a national academic meeting dedicated to advancing the treatment of valvular and structural heart diseases, in Chennai.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan launched the India Valve Registry during the India Valves 2026 conference in Chennai. He highlighted the importance of generating India-specific clinical evidence to strengthen cardiac research, improve medical decision-making and enhance… pic.twitter.com/1NLbaZy0E5
Addressing leading cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, researchers and medical experts from India and abroad, the Vice President said that the coming together of clinical expertise, scientific inquiry, innovation and collaboration represents an important step in the service of humanity.
He underlined that behind every medical procedure, clinical decision and scientific advancement is ultimately a human being, a patient who wishes to live longer, healthier and with dignity.
Highlighting the remarkable advances made in cardiovascular medicine, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan noted that while valvular and structural heart diseases remain an important and growing challenge, advances in medical science have transformed the way these conditions are treated.
He emphasised that every advancement in medical science brings with it a new responsibility to ensure that its benefits are inclusive and accessible to all. He said that healthcare is a human right and should be accessible to everyone.
The Vice President described the launch of the India Valve Registry as an important step in this direction. He said that a valve registry, by systematically recording information on patients undergoing heart valve interventions, their treatment and outcomes over time, can transform individual clinical experiences into collective medical knowledge.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan stressed the importance of generating India-specific clinical evidence. He noted that several countries have developed national registries for advanced valve interventions and other cardiovascular procedures and welcomed efforts to establish such a collaborative initiative in India.
He said that such registries would help create “our country’s own data for our own countrymen” and would enable the medical community to better understand outcomes, identify challenges and gaps, learn from experience and improve patient care.
The Vice President highlighted India’s growing stature as a centre of medical expertise and innovation. Referring to India’s achievements during the COVID-19 pandemic, he said that the country not only developed vaccines for its own people but also supplied vaccines to around 100 countries, demonstrating India’s growing medical and technological capabilities.
“Our doctors, scientists and healthcare professionals have earned respect across the world. India has demonstrated remarkable capabilities in advanced medical treatment,” he said.
Referring to the national goal of building a Viksit Bharat by 2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that a developed India must also be a Swasth Bharat.
Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan called for collective efforts to build a healthcare ecosystem in which innovation, technology and scientific progress are ultimately measured by their ability to improve human lives.
The event was attended by Tamil Nadu Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare Thiru K. G. Arunraj; Senior Interventional Cardiologist, Apollo hospitals, Chennai, Dr. G. Sengottuvelu;  Chairman, Cardiac Sciences, Fortis Escorts Heart Institute, New Delhi, Dr Ashok Seth; Chairman, Interventional Cardiology, Medanta–The Medicity, Gurugram, Dr. Praveen Chandra, besides eminent cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, researchers, scientists and members of the organising committee.
About India Valves 2026 & India Valve Registry
India Valves 2026 is a national academic meeting on valvular and structural heart disease, bringing together leading cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, researchers and healthcare professionals from across the country and abroad for scientific exchange, training and collaborative research.
The India Valve Registry is a collaborative multicentre initiative for systematic, secure and de-identified collection of real-world data on transcatheter valve interventions across India, aimed at strengthening India-specific clinical evidence and improving patient care.

title: Vice-President to visit Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh from September 6 to 9
text:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, will undertake a four-day visit to Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh from September 6 to 9, 2026. During his visit, the Vice-President will participate in a series of academic, cultural and public engagements, besides visiting institutions of historical, social and national significance. On September 6, the Vice-President will arrive in Guwahati, Assam. He will attend the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Geetanagar College, formerly known as Kanya Mahavidyalaya. He will later attend the Convocation Ceremony of Srimanta Sankaradeva University of Health Sciences (SSUHS), Guwahati. On September 7, the Vice-President will attend a foundation stone laying programme at Gauhati University, followed by an interaction with students, faculty members and leading citizens at the University’s Convention Centre. He will thereafter proceed to Shillong, Meghalaya, where he will attend a public reception and cultural programme at Soso Tham Auditorium. On September 8, the Vice-President will visit Imphal, Manipur. He will visit the INA Museum and War Memorial at Moirang and Sainik School Imphal. He will thereafter proceed to Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh. On September 9, the Vice-President will attend a special session of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly and visit the Assembly Gallery-cum-Museum. He will also visit Nyedar Namlo , Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum in Itanagar and the Donyi Polo Mission School for the hearing and visually impaired.

title: Vice President inaugurates Advanced Instrumentation Facility and Tech Innovation Forum at Panjab University, Chandigarh
text:
The Vice-President of India and Ex-officio Chancellor of Panjab University, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, visited Panjab University, Chandigarh today.During his visit, the Vice-President inaugurated the Advanced Instrumentation Facility at the Sophisticated Analytical Instrument Facility/Central Instrumentation Laboratories (SAIF/CIL). He also inaugurated the Panjab University Tech Innovation Forum (PU-TIF). SAIF/CIL and PU-TIF represent important components of the University's ecosystem for academic, applied and translational research, providing advanced analytical, incubation and entrepreneurial support to researchers, innovators and industry.
The Vice-President of India and Ex-officio Chancellor of Panjab University, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, visited Panjab University, Chandigarh today. The Vice-President inaugurated the Advanced Instrumentation Facility at the Sophisticated Analytical Instrument Facility/Central… pic.twitter.com/SStJVw1YTC
Addressing the gathering, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled the University’s distinguished legacy since its establishment in 1882 and noted its contribution to nation-building through generations of leaders, jurists, scientists, sportspersons and public servants.
Vice-President of India and Ex-Officio Chancellor of Panjab University, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, inaugurated advanced scientific infrastructure facilities at Panjab University, Chandigarh, today. He expressed confidence that these facilities and the Panjab University Tech… pic.twitter.com/g42GnrZVKv
The Vice-President said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Bharat’s higher education and scientific research ecosystem has undergone a transformative change. He observed that India is increasingly emerging as a global destination for quality education, research and innovation.
Describing the day’s inaugurations as two important milestones, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the installation of five advanced scientific instruments Atomic Force Microscope, Raman Spectrometer, DNA Sequencer, Flow Cytometer and FTIR Spectrometer, would significantly strengthen the University’s research capabilities in fields including nanotechnology, materials science, environmental science and genomics.
Highlighting the importance of innovation, the Vice-President said that the transformation of Bio-NEST into the Panjab University Tech Innovation Forum as a Section 8 not-for-profit company represents a new institutional framework for advancing research, entrepreneurship and technology development. He emphasised that innovation thrives when academia, industry, incubators and investors work together.
Addressing young researchers, he urged them to pursue science with purpose, remain resilient in the face of failure, and develop innovations that are inclusive, scalable and capable of addressing real societal needs. He said that research should have a meaningful impact on society. He called upon researchers and students to pursue research in the right direction so that its benefits reach society at large.
The Vice-President also addressed campus safety, stating that following the unfortunate death of a Ph.D. student, he had immediately directed the University authorities to undertake a comprehensive safety audit of the entire campus. He said an internal committee has been constituted to review the existing infrastructure and submit a detailed report, and stressed that the safety and well-being of students and staff must remain the University’s highest priority.

title: AIIMS Raipur symbolises Chhattisgarh’s journey from the fear of Left-Wing Extremism to peace, progress and opportunity: Vice President
text:
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the Third Convocation Ceremony of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Raipur, and called upon the graduating students to shoulder the responsibility of serving the health, trust and lives of the people of Bharat.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the 3rd Convocation of AIIMS Raipur today. He described AIIMS Raipur as a symbol of this transformation and highlighted its achievements in advanced healthcare, research and transplantation, including the State’s first swap kidney… pic.twitter.com/QMnhOqzMZX
Addressing the gathering, the Vice President said that a convocation is not merely a moment of celebration but also a moment of responsibility. “Today, you receive your degrees and tomorrow, you will be entrusted with something far more valuable-the health, trust and lives of the people of Bharat,” he said.
The Vice President highlighted the important role played by AIIMS Raipur since its establishment in 2012 in addressing regional disparities in healthcare, medical education and research, particularly in central India. He said that in a remarkably short period, the institution has evolved into a major tertiary-care institution serving Chhattisgarh and neighbouring states, including rural and tribal communities.
He noted that the growth of AIIMS Raipur reflects the remarkable transformation taking place in Chhattisgarh.
Referring to the challenges faced by parts of Chhattisgarh for decades, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said difficult geography, inadequate connectivity and Left-Wing Extremism had created serious obstacles to development. In many remote and tribal areas, fear and violence had disrupted the growth of roads, schools and hospitals, leaving communities facing distance and deprivation in accessing essential services.
The Vice President said that Chhattisgarh today has emerged from the shadows of its past and is witnessing a new dawn of prosperity, development and progress. He attributed this transformation to the decisive leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the strategic resolve of Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah and the committed leadership of Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai.
He said that the Naxal menace of decades has been brought to an end and areas once identified with violence are increasingly being identified with roads, schools, hospitals, connectivity, investment and opportunity.
“This transformation is a powerful example of the difference that strong political will, firm security policy and development-oriented governance can make,” he said.
The Vice President described AIIMS Raipur as one of the finest symbols of the new Chhattisgarh, which is moving from an era of fear and deprivation to an era of peace, progress and possibility.
He also appreciated the institute’s achievements in advanced healthcare and transplantation. He highlighted Chhattisgarh’s first swap kidney transplant, more than 95 per cent success in kidney transplantation, renal and corneal transplants and ear implants as significant achievements demonstrating how rapidly advanced medicine is becoming accessible in the region. He said the approval for a heart-transplant programme represents another important milestone.
Emphasising the importance of balanced development for achieving the national vision of Viksit Bharat, the Vice President said that the vision can be realised only when every state, district and village develops.
He said access to higher education is at the core of the vision of Viksit Bharat and highlighted the expansion of higher education during the last twelve years.
He also highlighted the significant increase in women’s participation in higher education, with female enrolment rising from 1.57 crore in 2014-15 to 2.24 crore in 2023-24, representing a 42.2 per cent increase. At the AIIMS Raipur convocation too, he noted that 376 women and 313 men are receiving degrees.
Addressing the graduates, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan called upon the young graduates to always say a firm “No to Drugs” and contribute to building a Bharat where technology reaches the last citizen and every young Bharatiya can aspire to a better future.
“May your knowledge heal, your research innovate and your service inspire,” the Vice President said.
He wished AIIMS Raipur continued success in clinical excellence, scientific innovation, public health and compassionate service. He also expressed the hope that the transformation of Chhattisgarh would become an important chapter in the larger journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.The Vice President also conferred gold medals and certificates on meritorious students.
Governor of Chhattisgarh Shri Ramen Deka, Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals & Fertilizers Smt. Anupriya Patel, Chhattisgarh Minister for Health & Family Welfare and Medical Education Shri Shyam Bihari Jaiswal, Raipur MP Shri Brijmohan Agrawal, President of AIIMS Raipur Prof. (Dr.) Sanjeev Handa and Executive Director AIIMS Raipur Retired Lieutenant General Ashok Jindal were present on the occasion.
*****

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi distributes more than 51,000 appointment letters to the newly appointed youth in Government at 20th Rozgar Mela
text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi distributed more than 51,000 appointment letters to newly appointed youth in various government organizations at the 20th Rozgar Mela today via video conferencing. Addressing on the occasion, he emphasized that this milestone brings immense joy to thousands of families, serving as a tribute to both the personal hard work of the candidates and the immense sacrifices made by their parents. "I wish you all the very best for this new beginning in life,” remarked Shri Modi.
Welcoming the new appointees into the Government of India as the nation marches toward the monumental milestone of a developed nation by 2047, the Prime Minister emphasized the pivotal role of youth in continuously empowering the twin campaigns of a developed and self-reliant India through every administrative decision. He highlighted their special responsibility toward fellow youth, noting that the talent and skills of the younger generation have captured the world's trust, fueling immense global expectations from Indian innovators, entrepreneurs, and youth power."The world has high hopes from our innovators, our entrepreneurs, and our youth power,” asserted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on the recently concluded BRICS Summit, the Prime Minister stated that the administration’s strategy is to expand international cooperation far beyond traditional government-to-government interactions. He explained that initiatives like BRICS CONNECT and the BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal are designed to integrate entrepreneurs, farmers, women, and the youth directly into global partnerships. "Everyone should become an active participant in this partnership,” noted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the economic diplomacy of the past few years, the Prime Minister pointed out that Free Trade Agreements with approximately 40 countries are unlocking unprecedented career possibilities. He emphasized that these agreements forge new markets and dynamic partnerships for domestic entrepreneurs while expanding career horizons for the youth. "These Free Trade Agreements are creating new doors of possibilities for our youth,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the government's sustained focus on future-ready skilling, the Prime Minister listed transformative initiatives such as the National Education Policy, the Skill India Mission, the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, and efforts to promote apprenticeships. He highlighted the PM-SETU scheme, which is modernizing one thousand government ITIs with an investment of 60,000 crore rupees alongside direct industry participation. "Our endeavor is that the education and skills of the youth keep pace with the needs of the changing economy,” asserted Shri Modi.
Praising the explosive growth of the domestic startup ecosystem, the Prime Minister celebrated the nation's position as the world's third-largest startup hub, noting that nearly half of recognized startups now hail from tier-two and tier-three cities. He commended the youth from smaller towns for actively working on their ideas, building companies, and generating new employment opportunities for their peers. "Today the youth from villages, towns, and small cities are also playing a major role in India's new economy,” observed Shri Modi.
Outlining the strategy to boost private sector employment, the Prime Minister highlighted the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana, a massive one lakh crore rupee initiative aiming to introduce two crore youths into the formal workforce for the first time. He detailed that the scheme offers up to 15,000 rupees in incentives for first-time employees while also financially rewarding employers who generate new jobs. "The government is working on every front to increase employment in the country,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Connecting job creation to robust macroeconomic health, the Prime Minister explained that new youth opportunities emerge only when the economy grows, investments increase, and new industries expand. He highlighted the nation's impressive 7.8 percent growth rate and a 12 percent surge in investments during the first quarter, noting that rating agencies are upgrading the nation's economic outlook despite pervasive global uncertainties. "The reforms of the past years have a major contribution behind this growth of India,” noted Shri Modi.
Directing the new officials to embrace an era of continuous administrative transformation, the Prime Minister stressed the critical need to simplify tax compliance, enhance the ease of doing business, implement reforms in education and skilling, and open new sectors to innovation. He tasked the young bureaucrats with ensuring that the momentum of governance improvements remains unstoppable throughout their tenures. "It is necessary that the Reform Express in the country runs continuously at full speed,” asserted Shri Modi.
Invoking his poetic remarks about claiming the sun, the sea, the boat, and the sailor to conquer the waves, the Prime Minister challenged the new recruits to match this courage by championing the deep aspirations of the country's youth. He insisted that every file signature and every administrative decision must actively clear hurdles, allow ideas to flourish, and promote innovation-driven investment that ultimately creates employment. "Your signature on every file should be one that advances youth aspirations,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Appealing to their personal journeys, the Prime Minister urged the fresh appointees to utilize their new authority within the government system with deep empathy. He advised them to actively dismantle the bureaucratic hurdles they themselves faced before joining the service. "Your effort should be that the difficulties you have gone through, other youths should not have to go through them,” remarked Shri Modi.
Encouraging a mindset of lifelong learning in a rapidly changing world, the Prime Minister directed the recruits to continuously upgrade their skills and master new technologies through the Mission Karmayogi framework. He noted that the 'Karmayogi Prarambh' module has been specifically designed to help new entrants navigate the system, joining the 1.7 crore employees already on the iGOT platform. "The more you improve yourself, the better you will be able to serve the citizens of the country,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Emphasizing that the true strength of any government lies in public trust, the Prime Minister reminded the recruits that their daily work, from processing elderly pensions to student scholarships and farmer subsidies, directly impacts common lives. He stressed that their behavior, efficiency, honesty, and sensitivity will ultimately define the citizen's personal experience with the state. "Your behavior, your sensitivity, your efficiency, your honesty, all this will determine what that citizen's experience with the government is like,” observed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address with a powerful administrative mantra, the Prime Minister called upon the new officials to adopt the philosophy of 'Nagrik Devo Bhava' (The Citizen is Divine) in their daily service, equating citizen service to national service. He expressed his unwavering belief that they will fulfill their duties with utmost dedication and service across all departments. "Your success will be even greater when your work makes a citizen's life easier,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM’s remarks during 20th Rozgar Mela via video conferencing
text:
My dear young companions,
The festive season has begun in the country. Amidst these celebrations, today brings a new joy into the lives of thousands of families. Today, more than 51,000 youth across the nation are receiving appointment letters for government service. Behind the achievement you have reached today is not only your hard work, but also the dedication of your parents and family members. I extend heartfelt congratulations to all of you and your families. I wish you all the best for this new beginning in life.
Friends,
Today you are joining the Government of India at a time when the nation is moving towards a very big goal - the goal of making India developed by 2047. In this, the role of youth like you is immense. While serving in government, you must take every decision that strengthens the campaign for a developed India and for self‑reliant India. As youth, you have a special responsibility towards other young people. You can see how the talent and skills of our youth have won the trust of the entire world. The world has great expectations from our innovators, entrepreneurs, and youth power. Just a few days ago, the BRICS Summit concluded. India’s effort has been that BRICS cooperation should not remain limited to governments alone - our entrepreneurs, farmers, women, youth, everyone should become active participants in this partnership. With this vision, initiatives like BRICS CONNECT and the BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal have been launched.
Friends,
In recent years, India has signed free trade agreements with nearly 40 countries. These FTAs are opening new doors of opportunity for our youth. Such trade agreements create new partnerships for our entrepreneurs, open new markets, and create new career possibilities for our youth.
Friends,
In recent years, the Government of India has consistently focused on preparing youth for the future. The National Education Policy, Skill India Mission, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, and efforts to promote apprenticeships - all aim to ensure that the education and skills of our youth align with the needs of a changing economy. One example is PM‑SETU. Through this scheme, with an investment of 60,000 crore rupees, 1,000 government ITIs are being modernized. Direct participation of industry has been ensured in this.
Friends,
Another picture of the strength of India’s youth is visible in our startup ecosystem. Today India is the world’s third‑largest startup ecosystem. And India’s startup story is no longer just about big cities. Today, nearly half of recognized startups are in tier‑two and tier‑three cities. That means youth from villages, towns, and small cities are also playing a big role in India’s new economy. Our young people from smaller towns are working on their ideas, building new companies, and creating new employment opportunities for other youth as well.
Friends,
Our effort is that new employment opportunities also grow rapidly in the private sector. With this vision, the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana has been launched. About 1 lakh crore rupees are being spent on this scheme. With its help, nearly 20 million youth will get the chance to join the workforce for the first time. Under this scheme, the government is giving an incentive of up to 15,000 rupees to youth who get their first job. Employers who create new jobs are also being encouraged by the government. That means the government is working on every front to increase employment in the country.
Friends,
New opportunities for youth are created only when the country’s economy grows, when investment increases, new industries are set up, and new sectors expand. Today India is one of the fastest‑growing major economies. In the first quarter of this financial year, India’s growth rate was 7.8 percent. Investment increased by nearly 12 percent. Rating agencies are upgrading India’s ratings. And this progress is happening at a time when the world is passing through many uncertainties. Behind India’s growth is the major contribution of reforms carried out in recent years. In your tenure, you must continue to accelerate reforms. Whether it is simplifying tax and compliance, increasing ease of doing business, reforms in education and skilling, opening new sectors for innovation, or ease of living - at every level, the Reform Express must continue at full speed. And as government employees, you will have a very big role in this in the present and coming years.
Friends,
I said a few days ago - the sun must be ours, the sea must be ours. The boat must be ours, the sailor must be ours. The courage to write victory on the waves must be ours. Today India’s youth are moving forward with this courage. Now, while serving in the Government of India, it is your responsibility to understand the aspirations of the country’s youth and fulfill your duties accordingly. I urge you again - every decision you take, every signature you put on a file, must advance the aspirations of youth. In your tenure, you must ensure that obstacles in the path of youth are removed, their ideas get opportunities to move forward, innovation increases investment, and investment creates new employment opportunities.
Friends,
Now you are becoming part of the government system yourselves. Therefore, your effort must be that the difficulties you faced, or that your parents faced, should not be faced by other youth. The hardships your parents endured, the hardships you may have endured - no citizen of our country should have to endure them anymore. This is the work you must do as soon as you enter the government system.
Friends,
Today, transformation is happening rapidly in every sector of the country. You have reached here by continuously learning. Now from here begins a new journey of continuous learning. You must keep improving your skills. You must understand new technologies and new systems. Mission Karmayogi helps you achieve this very purpose. More than 17 million government employees are connected to the iGOT Karmayogi platform today. And for new companions like you, Karmayogi Prarambh has been specially designed. The more you improve yourself, the better you will serve the citizens of the country.
Friends,
You must always remember one more thing. The real strength of government is the trust of the country’s citizens. Whatever ministry you are in, whatever department you are in, your work will touch the life of ordinary citizens in some way. A pension for an elderly person may move forward because of your work. A scholarship for a student may depend on your responsibility. A facility for a farmer may be delivered through your department. For some citizen, you may be the face of the government. Your behavior, your sensitivity, your efficiency, your honesty - all these will determine how that citizen experiences the government.
Therefore, friends,
In government service, our mantra must be - Citizen Devo Bhava, Citizen Devo Bhava. Service to citizens is service to the nation. Your success will be greater when your work makes life easier for a citizen. I am confident that wherever you are, in whichever department you are, you will continue to fulfill your duties with dedication and a spirit of service. Once again, I congratulate you all.
Thank you very much.
MJPS/SS/VJ/ST

Our effort is that new employment opportunities also grow rapidly in the private sector. With this vision, the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana has been launched. About 1 lakh crore rupees are being spent on this scheme. With its help, nearly 20 million youth will get the chance to join the workforce for the first time. Under this scheme, the government is giving an incentive of up to 15,000 rupees to youth who get their first job. Employers who create new jobs are also being encouraged by the government. That means the government is working on every front to increase employment in the country.
Friends,
New opportunities for youth are created only when the country’s economy grows, when investment increases, new industries are set up, and new sectors expand. Today India is one of the fastest‑growing major economies. In the first quarter of this financial year, India’s growth rate was 7.8 percent. Investment increased by nearly 12 percent. Rating agencies are upgrading India’s ratings. And this progress is happening at a time when the world is passing through many uncertainties. Behind India’s growth is the major contribution of reforms carried out in recent years. In your tenure, you must continue to accelerate reforms. Whether it is simplifying tax and compliance, increasing ease of doing business, reforms in education and skilling, opening new sectors for innovation, or ease of living - at every level, the Reform Express must continue at full speed. And as government employees, you will have a very big role in this in the present and coming years.
Friends,
I said a few days ago - the sun must be ours, the sea must be ours. The boat must be ours, the sailor must be ours. The courage to write victory on the waves must be ours. Today India’s youth are moving forward with this courage. Now, while serving in the Government of India, it is your responsibility to understand the aspirations of the country’s youth and fulfill your duties accordingly. I urge you again - every decision you take, every signature you put on a file, must advance the aspirations of youth. In your tenure, you must ensure that obstacles in the path of youth are removed, their ideas get opportunities to move forward, innovation increases investment, and investment creates new employment opportunities.
Friends,
Now you are becoming part of the government system yourselves. Therefore, your effort must be that the difficulties you faced, or that your parents faced, should not be faced by other youth. The hardships your parents endured, the hardships you may have endured - no citizen of our country should have to endure them anymore. This is the work you must do as soon as you enter the government system.
Friends,
Today, transformation is happening rapidly in every sector of the country. You have reached here by continuously learning. Now from here begins a new journey of continuous learning. You must keep improving your skills. You must understand new technologies and new systems. Mission Karmayogi helps you achieve this very purpose. More than 17 million government employees are connected to the iGOT Karmayogi platform today. And for new companions like you, Karmayogi Prarambh has been specially designed. The more you improve yourself, the better you will serve the citizens of the country.
Friends,
You must always remember one more thing. The real strength of government is the trust of the country’s citizens. Whatever ministry you are in, whatever department you are in, your work will touch the life of ordinary citizens in some way. A pension for an elderly person may move forward because of your work. A scholarship for a student may depend on your responsibility. A facility for a farmer may be delivered through your department. For some citizen, you may be the face of the government. Your behavior, your sensitivity, your efficiency, your honesty - all these will determine how that citizen experiences the government.
Therefore, friends,
In government service, our mantra must be - Citizen Devo Bhava, Citizen Devo Bhava. Service to citizens is service to the nation. Your success will be greater when your work makes life easier for a citizen. I am confident that wherever you are, in whichever department you are, you will continue to fulfill your duties with dedication and a spirit of service. Once again, I congratulate you all.
Thank you very much.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”
text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” today at Vigyan Bhawan in New Delhi. Addressing the occasion, the Prime Minister highlighted the nation's profound historical connection to nature, emphasizing how ancient cultural wisdom is actively shaping modern climate solutions and inspiring global collective action. He commended the National Green Tribunal for steadfastly advancing this critical mission and extended his congratulations to the organizers. “India is now providing solutions to modern climate challenges,” asserted Shri Modi.
Addressing the flawed global narrative regarding carbon footprints, the Prime Minister pointed out that developing nations are unjustly blamed, despite developed nations emitting up to six times more carbon per capita than India. He detailed how the nation uses international platforms to assert this historical truth and showcase its traditional environmental strengths, recalling the launch of the "Convenient Action- Continuity for Change" book at COP-21 and the creation of platforms like One Sun, One World, One Grid, the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, the Global Biofuel Alliance, and the International Big Cat Alliance. "We are establishing new benchmarks for environmental protection by taking the world along,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Bridging ancient philosophy with modern execution, the Prime Minister detailed the extraordinary progress made across every environmental sector over the past dozen years, specifically highlighting a massive strategic pivot toward renewable energy. He proudly stated that the nation proudly occupies a unique position within the G-20 for having achieved its COP-21 commitments ahead of schedule, setting global benchmarks in non-fossil fuels and solar capacity. "India's performance on every parameter is a topic of discussion in the world today,” noted Shri Modi.
Presenting stark evidence of the nation's solar revolution, the Prime Minister cited the leap from a mere 2 gigawatts of capacity a dozen years ago to over 160 gigawatts today, fueled by the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana which has solarized over 50 lakh homes with financial assistance of up to 80,000 rupees per household. He added that 30 lakh farmers have received solar pumps under the Kusum Yojana, while the completed One Nation-One Grid project has successfully prevented 200 million tonnes of carbon emissions. "We have started a mission to make homes themselves the center of solar power generation,” asserted Shri Modi.
Expanding on the massive strides in the broader clean energy landscape, the Prime Minister highlighted the threefold increase in wind capacity, significant hydro expansions, and a newly energized focus on nuclear power generation that now welcomes private players. He noted that these combined efforts have nearly quadrupled the nation's non-fossil energy capacity while advancing cleaner technologies like Coal Gasification. "India has achieved major milestones in other sectors of clean energy as well,” noted Shri Modi.
Celebrating the dawn of advanced clean mobility, the Prime Minister proudly announced the recent launch of the country's first Hydrogen Train, which also holds the record as the world's longest. He described this technological leap as a foundational milestone for the future of green transportation. "This is the beginning of a new era of clean mobility,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the massive adoption of green vehicles, the Prime Minister highlighted a staggering 950-fold increase in Electric Vehicles, jumping from under three thousand sales before 2014 to roughly 25 lakh last year. He also pointed out that the modern FASTag system on highways and expressways has drastically reduced fuel wastage by minimizing wait times at toll booths. "India is embracing this opportunity of the EV revolution with full force,” noted Shri Modi.
Showcasing the sweeping modernization of public transport infrastructure, the Prime Minister contrasted the meager five-city, 250-kilometer metro network of 2014 with today's expansive system operating in over 20 cities. "India has joined the ranks of those countries in the world that have a metro network of more than a thousand kilometers,” asserted Shri Modi.
Underscoring the eco-friendly transformation of heavy logistics, the Prime Minister explained how the near-total electrification of the railways has saved crores of liters of diesel from being burned. He highlighted the massive environmental benefits of the newly inaugurated 3,000-kilometer Dedicated Freight Corridor, where historic double-stack container trains are replacing hundreds of polluting trucks per journey. "You can imagine on what a large scale this is helping the environment,” observed Shri Modi.
Pointing to alternative eco-friendly transport modes, the Prime Minister celebrated the operationalization of approximately 5,000 kilometers of inland waterways across the country. He explained that a single standard inland vessel navigating these routes can carry a load equivalent to dozens of trucks. "This too is providing great help in environmental conservation,” noted Shri Modi.
Summarizing the collective impact of these transit upgrades, the Prime Minister emphasized that the sweeping changes across the entire mobility sector serve as undeniable proof of the nation's balanced growth trajectory. He stated that rapid progress is entirely compatible with environmental preservation. "Our development is speedy as well as sustainable,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Praising the unprecedented mass participation in water conservation, the Prime Minister celebrated the construction of over 70,000 Amrit Sarovars and 1.5 crore rainwater harvesting structures under the Catch the Rain campaign. He noted that modern irrigation techniques under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana and 'Per Drop, More Crop' are actively saving water for over 2 crore farmers. "Unprecedented work is being done on water conservation in India,” noted Shri Modi.
Championing the global revival of millets, the Prime Minister explained how promoting the cultivation of water-efficient Shree Anna has boosted domestic production and increased exports to 1.5 lakh tons, simultaneously creating economic opportunities and conserving water. He credited these relentless national efforts for inspiring the global celebration of 2023 as the International Year of Millets. "Because of this model, the world is also joining us,” remarked Shri Modi.'
Underscoring the massive scale of ecological agriculture, the Prime Minister detailed the establishment of 24,000 natural farming clusters across 12.5 lakh hectares under the National Mission on Natural Farming. He also highlighted the successful development of 3,000 climate-resilient crop varieties and the strategic promotion of agro-forestry to reduce the national footprint. "By promoting agro-forestry, we are also reducing carbon footprints,” asserted Shri Modi.
Illustrating the comprehensive nature of the country's environmental efforts, the Prime Minister shared that the very dense forest cover has increased by more than 22 percent over the last 12 years. He praised the ongoing 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign for inspiring citizens to plant crores of trees in a continuous, nationwide drive. Addressing the critical challenge of plastic pollution, the Prime Minister reiterated the national ban on single-use plastics and the strong push toward a Circular Economy based on reducing, reusing, and recycling thousands of tons of daily waste. He cited the Gobardhan Yojana as a prime example of converting rural organic waste into valuable resources through a Wealth from Waste model. "Our endeavor is that instead of treating waste as a problem, it should be transformed into a resource,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Elevating the significance of the nation's environmental achievements, the Prime Minister stated that these robust statistics represent far more than domestic progress. He framed the nation's developmental data as monumental, direct contributions to the survival and prosperity of the entire human race. "These are also figures of India's contribution to the future of humanity,” asserted Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister underscored the profound relationship between the earth and its inhabitants that drives these responsible actions. He concluded his address on an optimistic note, expressing deep confidence that the conference deliberations would yield innovative solutions, and offered his final felicitations. "India is also working to build a responsible and sustainable future,” affirmed Shri Modi.
India is showing how development and environmental sustainability can go hand in hand. Speaking at the International Conference on "The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics." https://t.co/QTmc4v8yeT

title: English rendering of PM’s address at the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”
text:
Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant ji, my colleague in the Union Cabinet Bhupender Yadav ji, Attorney General of India R. Venkataramani ji, National Green Tribunal (NGT) Chairman Justice Prakash Srivastava ji, all distinguished dignitaries present in this hall, ladies and gentlemen.
For centuries, India has guided the world on the subject of nature and environment. With that ideological commitment, and based on our cultural experiences, India is now also providing solutions to modern climate challenges, while at the same time calling for collective efforts of humanity. I am happy that this NGT conference is carrying forward that mission. For this event, I extend my congratulations and best wishes to all the officials of NGT and all dignitaries associated with it.
Friends,
We all know that often the responsibility for carbon emissions has been wrongly placed on developing countries. Many of my companions from the Global South are present here. But the historical truth is that even today, India’s per capita carbon emissions are less than half the global average. In developed countries, per capita carbon emissions are six times higher than India’s. Six times higher. India presents this fact strongly on global platforms. And I say to every Indian - show your strength too. We have also presented our traditions and their power before the world. On these very subjects, during COP‑21 in Paris, we launched the book Convenient Action – Continuity for Change. We are establishing new benchmarks for environmental protection by taking the world along. Whether it is the vision of One Sun, One World, One Grid, or the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, Global Biofuel Alliance, International Big Cat Alliance, Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) - each of these platforms is becoming a stage for India’s dedicated commitments on climate and environment.
Friends,
Today’s India is moving forward by weaving its ancient ideas of environmental protection into a modern vision. In the past 12 years, India has made extraordinary progress in every sector related to the environment. Our major focus has been on renewable energy, and this has played a big role in environmental protection. India is the only country in the G20 - I say this before the big leaders of the G20 - the only country that has fulfilled all the commitments it made at the COP‑21 summit in Paris, and has done so ahead of schedule. This is the strength of Hindustan that I am talking about. On every parameter - non‑fossil fuel, solar energy capacity, curbing carbon emissions - India’s performance is today a subject of positive discussion worldwide. Look at the figures. Twelve years ago, India’s solar energy capacity was about 2 gigawatts. Twelve years ago - 2 gigawatts. If there are lawyers here, please note these figures, they may come in handy. Today it has crossed 160 gigawatts. From 2 gigawatts to 160 gigawatts in 12 years. Under the PM Surya Ghar Free Electricity Scheme, we launched the mission to make homes themselves centers of solar power generation. Under this scheme, more than 5 million homes have already installed rooftop solar panels. This is more than the total number of homes in many countries. For this, the government has provided financial assistance of up to 80,000 rupees per household. Under the KUSUM scheme, the government has installed solar pumps in the fields of 3 million farmers. We have also completed the ambitious One Nation, One Grid project. Not only this - LED bulbs in homes have proven successful in saving electricity. Crores of LED bulbs have been distributed to households. And the results of these efforts are before us today. From solar energy alone, India has succeeded in preventing nearly 200 million tonnes of carbon emissions.
Friends,
Along with solar energy, India has also achieved major accomplishments in other clean energy sectors. In the past 12 years, the country’s wind energy capacity has tripled. Hydropower capacity has increased significantly. And now the country is working rapidly on nuclear energy generation. Those who give long speeches on the environment - when I advance nuclear energy work, they will stand in the courts to stop it. A pathway has also been created to bring private players into this sector. Because of these efforts, today India’s non‑fossil energy capacity has nearly quadrupled. India is also promoting technologies like coal gasification for cleaner use of coal.
Friends,
India is now working rapidly in areas like clean mobility and green hydrogen. Just a few days ago, India’s first hydrogen train was launched - and it is the world’s longest hydrogen train. This marks the beginning of a new era of clean mobility.
Friends,
In 12 years, the number of electric vehicles in our country has increased nearly 950 times. 950 times. In the year before 2014, fewer than 3,000 EVs were sold in India. Last year, nearly 2.5 million EVs were sold in India. That means India is embracing the opportunity of the EV revolution with full strength, and this is also helping the environment. On our highways and expressways, modern fast‑track systems have reduced waiting at toll booths. This has stopped the fuel wastage that used to occur at toll booths.
Friends,
Until 2014, in five cities of our country there was less than 250 kilometers of metro network. Lawyers here should note this figure. Before 2014, only five cities had less than 250 kilometers. Today, metros run in more than 20 cities, and India has joined the countries with more than 1,000 kilometers of metro network.
Friends,
With nearly 100 percent electrification of railways, billions of liters of diesel burning has been avoided. The environment has been protected. Just this month, a 3,000‑kilometer‑long Dedicated Freight Corridor was inaugurated. Every train running on it carries loads equal to hundreds of trucks from one place to another. The operation of double‑stack container freight trains is historic in itself. You can imagine how greatly this helps the environment.
Friends,
Today, transportation is happening on about 5,000 kilometers of waterways in the country. This is the most environment‑friendly mobility. A standard inland vessel running on these waterways carries loads equal to dozens of trucks in one journey. This too is greatly helping environmental protection.
Friends,
All these changes in the mobility sector alone are proof that our development is both speedy and sustainable.
Friends,
Today, with the participation of millions of people, unprecedented work is happening in India on water conservation. I am happy that more than 70,000 Amrit Sarovars have been constructed in the country. Under the Catch the Rain campaign, nearly 15 million water harvesting structures have been built, preserving rainwater. Through the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana, more than 20 million farmers today are connected with modern irrigation facilities. Initiatives like Per Drop More Crop are also saving water. Shri Anna - that is, millets - are another great successful example. India is promoting the cultivation of millets, which consume less water. In recent years, millet production has increased in the country, and exports have risen to about 150,000 tonnes. This is creating new opportunities for farmers, while also saving water. And because of this model, the world is joining us. Thanks to India’s efforts, 2023 was celebrated as the International Year of Millets.
Friends,
Under the National Mission on Natural Farming, today about 1.25 million hectares in the country have developed 24,000 clusters of natural farming. Not only this, nearly 3,000 varieties of climate‑resilient crops have also been developed in the country. By promoting agro‑forestry, we are also reducing carbon footprints.
Friends,
How wide‑ranging our efforts are can be seen in India’s forest coverage. This too I mention for my lawyer friends. In the past 12 years, our very dense forest cover has increased by more than 22 percent. This is a very big achievement. Under the campaign Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam (One Tree in the Name of Mother), crores of trees have been planted across the country. And this campaign continues.
Friends,
Plastic waste has also been a major challenge for the environment. That is why India has banned single‑use plastic. With the mantra of reduce, reuse, and recycle, we have promoted the circular economy. Today, thousands of tonnes of waste are being recycled every day in India. Through the Gobardhan Yojana, cow dung and other organic waste in villages are being converted into useful resources. Our effort is that waste should not be seen as a problem, but transformed into a resource under the Waste to Wealth model.
Friends,
All these figures are not just India’s development statistics - they are India’s contributions for the future of humanity.
Friends,
Our cultural thought is - “Mata bhumih, putro aham prithivyah” - meaning, this earth is our mother and we are her children. With this thinking, India is working to build a responsible and sustainable future. I am confident that the discussions in this conference, and the new ideas and solutions that emerge from it, may become a great support for future generations. Once again, I extend my many best wishes to all of you for this conference. Thank you very much.
****

In the past 12 years, India has made extraordinary progress in every sector related to the environment. Our major focus has been on renewable energy, and this has played a big role in environmental protection. India is the only country in the G20 - I say this before the big leaders of the G20 - the only country that has fulfilled all the commitments it made at the COP‑21 summit in Paris, and has done so ahead of schedule. This is the strength of Hindustan that I am talking about. On every parameter - non‑fossil fuel, solar energy capacity, curbing carbon emissions - India’s performance is today a subject of positive discussion worldwide. Look at the figures. Twelve years ago, India’s solar energy capacity was about 2 gigawatts. Twelve years ago - 2 gigawatts. If there are lawyers here, please note these figures, they may come in handy. Today it has crossed 160 gigawatts. From 2 gigawatts to 160 gigawatts in 12 years. Under the PM Surya Ghar Free Electricity Scheme, we launched the mission to make homes themselves centers of solar power generation. Under this scheme, more than 5 million homes have already installed rooftop solar panels. This is more than the total number of homes in many countries. For this, the government has provided financial assistance of up to 80,000 rupees per household. Under the KUSUM scheme, the government has installed solar pumps in the fields of 3 million farmers. We have also completed the ambitious One Nation, One Grid project. Not only this - LED bulbs in homes have proven successful in saving electricity. Crores of LED bulbs have been distributed to households. And the results of these efforts are before us today. From solar energy alone, India has succeeded in preventing nearly 200 million tonnes of carbon emissions.
Friends,
Along with solar energy, India has also achieved major accomplishments in other clean energy sectors. In the past 12 years, the country’s wind energy capacity has tripled. Hydropower capacity has increased significantly. And now the country is working rapidly on nuclear energy generation. Those who give long speeches on the environment - when I advance nuclear energy work, they will stand in the courts to stop it. A pathway has also been created to bring private players into this sector. Because of these efforts, today India’s non‑fossil energy capacity has nearly quadrupled. India is also promoting technologies like coal gasification for cleaner use of coal.
Friends,
India is now working rapidly in areas like clean mobility and green hydrogen. Just a few days ago, India’s first hydrogen train was launched - and it is the world’s longest hydrogen train. This marks the beginning of a new era of clean mobility.
Friends,
In 12 years, the number of electric vehicles in our country has increased nearly 950 times. 950 times. In the year before 2014, fewer than 3,000 EVs were sold in India. Last year, nearly 2.5 million EVs were sold in India. That means India is embracing the opportunity of the EV revolution with full strength, and this is also helping the environment. On our highways and expressways, modern fast‑track systems have reduced waiting at toll booths. This has stopped the fuel wastage that used to occur at toll booths.
Friends,
Until 2014, in five cities of our country there was less than 250 kilometers of metro network. Lawyers here should note this figure. Before 2014, only five cities had less than 250 kilometers. Today, metros run in more than 20 cities, and India has joined the countries with more than 1,000 kilometers of metro network.
Friends,
With nearly 100 percent electrification of railways, billions of liters of diesel burning has been avoided. The environment has been protected. Just this month, a 3,000‑kilometer‑long Dedicated Freight Corridor was inaugurated. Every train running on it carries loads equal to hundreds of trucks from one place to another. The operation of double‑stack container freight trains is historic in itself. You can imagine how greatly this helps the environment.
Friends,
Today, transportation is happening on about 5,000 kilometers of waterways in the country. This is the most environment‑friendly mobility. A standard inland vessel running on these waterways carries loads equal to dozens of trucks in one journey. This too is greatly helping environmental protection.
Friends,
All these changes in the mobility sector alone are proof that our development is both speedy and sustainable.
Friends,
Today, with the participation of millions of people, unprecedented work is happening in India on water conservation. I am happy that more than 70,000 Amrit Sarovars have been constructed in the country. Under the Catch the Rain campaign, nearly 15 million water harvesting structures have been built, preserving rainwater. Through the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana, more than 20 million farmers today are connected with modern irrigation facilities. Initiatives like Per Drop More Crop are also saving water. Shri Anna - that is, millets - are another great successful example. India is promoting the cultivation of millets, which consume less water. In recent years, millet production has increased in the country, and exports have risen to about 150,000 tonnes. This is creating new opportunities for farmers, while also saving water. And because of this model, the world is joining us. Thanks to India’s efforts, 2023 was celebrated as the International Year of Millets.
Friends,
Under the National Mission on Natural Farming, today about 1.25 million hectares in the country have developed 24,000 clusters of natural farming. Not only this, nearly 3,000 varieties of climate‑resilient crops have also been developed in the country. By promoting agro‑forestry, we are also reducing carbon footprints.
Friends,
How wide‑ranging our efforts are can be seen in India’s forest coverage. This too I mention for my lawyer friends. In the past 12 years, our very dense forest cover has increased by more than 22 percent. This is a very big achievement. Under the campaign Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam (One Tree in the Name of Mother), crores of trees have been planted across the country. And this campaign continues.
Friends,
Plastic waste has also been a major challenge for the environment. That is why India has banned single‑use plastic. With the mantra of reduce, reuse, and recycle, we have promoted the circular economy. Today, thousands of tonnes of waste are being recycled every day in India. Through the Gobardhan Yojana, cow dung and other organic waste in villages are being converted into useful resources. Our effort is that waste should not be seen as a problem, but transformed into a resource under the Waste to Wealth model.
Friends,
All these figures are not just India’s development statistics - they are India’s contributions for the future of humanity.
Friends,
Our cultural thought is - “Mata bhumih, putro aham prithivyah” - meaning, this earth is our mother and we are her children. With this thinking, India is working to build a responsible and sustainable future. I am confident that the discussions in this conference, and the new ideas and solutions that emerge from it, may become a great support for future generations. Once again, I extend my many best wishes to all of you for this conference. Thank you very much.
****
MJPS/SS/VJ/ST

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi receives a telephone call from the President of the UAE
text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi received a telephone call from His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the United Arab Emirates.
The UAE President conveyed warm greetings on the Prime Minister’s birthday.
The two leaders discussed new measures to further deepen the India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including in the areas of energy, defence, technology, investment and health.
The UAE President congratulated the Prime Minister on India’s successful BRICS Presidency. Prime Minister appreciated the participation of His Highness Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled in the BRICS Summit and the UAE’s cooperation and partnership in achieving substantive outcomes under India’s Presidency.
The two leaders exchanged views on developments in West Asia. They reaffirmed their commitment to continued cooperation and coordination in efforts to promote regional peace, security and stability.

title: Under 20th Rozgar Mela, PM to distribute more than 51,000 appointment letters to the newly appointed youth in Government on 19 September
text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will distribute more than 51,000 appointment letters to newly appointed youth in various Government Organisations at the 20th Rozgar Mela on 19 September 2026 at 12:30 PM via video conferencing. He will also address the newly selected candidates on the occasion.
This Rozgar Mela will be held at 45 locations across the country. The newly recruited candidates will be joining various Ministries and Departments of the Government of India including Department of Revenue, Ministry of Railways, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Defence among others.
Rozgar Mela reflects the Government’s continued focus on creating employment opportunities for the youth and ensuring their greater participation in the country’s development journey. With the 20th Rozgar Mela, a total of about 12.75 lakh youth will have received appointment letters in various Departments and Government Organisations.

title: PM to inaugurate International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” on 19 September
text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” on 19 September 2026 at around 10 AM at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.
The two-day Conference is being organised by the National Green Tribunal on 19 and 20 September 2026. It will witness the participation of environmental experts, Judges of the Supreme Court of India and High Courts, District Court Judges, Secretaries of various Ministries, senior government officials, representatives of State Judicial Academies, State Legal Services Authorities, State Expert Appraisal Committees (SEACs), State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities (SEIAAs), State Wetland Authorities and other stakeholders. It will also bring together eminent Judges and judicial representatives from 17 countries.
The Conference will provide a platform for the exchange of judicial approaches, scientific knowledge, environmental governance practices and institutional experiences across jurisdictions. It will facilitate dialogue on critical environmental and climate challenges, including gaps in policy formulation, implementation and enforcement, and explore ways to strengthen environmental governance and institutional cooperation.

He emphasized that their unwavering trust and affinity serve as a massive source of personal empowerment. "Your trust is my strength!” remarked Shri Modi.
Acknowledging the cultural significance of the day, the Prime Minister took a moment to celebrate a sacred festival dedicated to creation and craftsmanship. He extended his warmest greetings to all the citizens honoring this special occasion. "I extend my heartiest greetings to all of you on Vishwakarma Puja,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Highlighting the dawn of a transformative era in the state, the Prime Minister celebrated the introduction of a new tradition designed to empower local women through the Annapurna Yojana. He extended his heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to every female beneficiary stepping into this new chapter of capability. "Today, new capabilities have been added to the mothers and sisters of Bengal,” noted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on the immense domestic responsibilities shouldered by women, the Prime Minister acknowledged how they meticulously manage families through countless daily decisions. He pointed out that alleviating their financial anxieties regarding essential expenses naturally elevates their self-assurance. "When they have less worry about necessary expenses, their self-confidence increases even more,” observed Shri Modi.
Describing the Annapurna Yojana as a crucial intervention to bolster female confidence, the Prime Minister detailed how a guaranteed monthly deposit provides profound life support. He noted that receiving this fixed amount without having to ask anyone ensures financial dignity for the women. "This is a huge support for their lives. This is a big help!” asserted Shri Modi.
Presenting the tangible impact of the initiative, the Prime Minister announced that the fourth installment of 3,000 rupees is successfully reaching the bank accounts of approximately 1.5 crore sisters. He explained that this recurring financial assistance serves as a vital lifeline for purchasing medicines, household necessities, or funding a child's education. "For a sister, it could be a support to buy medicine or essential household items,” noted Shri Modi
Outlining the broader vision behind the financial assistance, the Prime Minister stated his firm belief in endowing women with robust decision-making power and the courage to advance. He congratulated the beneficiaries while reaffirming the central role the Annapurna scheme plays in this empowerment strategy. "The women of Bengal should also have the power of decision-making and the courage to move forward,” asserted Shri Modi.' The Prime Minister credited the mothers and sisters of the state for playing the most pivotal role in ushering in political change after enduring numerous hardships. He emphasized that the new government’s primary benchmark is to improve their Ease of Living by adhering strictly to the mantra of 'Less talk, more work'. "The very first test before our new government was to make the lives of Bengal's women easier,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the rapid execution of the welfare agenda, the Prime Minister highlighted that work on the Annapurna Yojana commenced within days of the new government taking office. He celebrated the seamless, direct bank transfers reaching millions of women while strictly eliminating corrupt practices.Underscoring the administration's commitment to absolute inclusivity, the Prime Minister assured that rapid efforts are underway to guarantee comprehensive coverage across the state. "It is also the goal of our government that not a single eligible woman should be deprived of the benefits of the Annapurna Yojana,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing a comprehensive lifecycle approach to female empowerment, the Prime Minister listed a multitude of prioritized interventions ranging from the Matru Vandana Yojana for pregnant women to the Beti Bachao - Beti Padhao movement. He enumerated sweeping initiatives, including building crores of school toilets, opening Sainik Schools for girls, providing Mudra loans, increasing maternity leave, delivering Ujjwala gas and Har Ghar Jal water connections, distributing Ayushman cards, and securing joint property rights under PM Awas, to comprehensively address every challenge faced by women from childhood through motherhood. "Solving every problem related to the life cycle of mothers, sisters, and daughters has been the highest priority,” asserted Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister assured the public that the current administration is rapidly accelerating these previously stalled programs to ensure timely delivery. "Now, under the present government, these stalled schemes have been taken forward at a rapid pace,” noted Shri Modi.
Citing the PM Awas Yojana as a prime example of renewed momentum, the Prime Minister announced that over 50 lakh newly identified poor families in the state will soon receive permanent houses, alongside the rollout of the PM Vishwakarma Yojana. He attributed this revival of pending projects to the overwhelming blessings and support of the local women, projecting a collaborative vision for the state's future. "We will all together build a new Bengal,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Linking regional progress to the national vision, the Prime Minister expressed absolute confidence that local women will continue to accelerate the development journey toward a Viksit Bharat. He emphasized that the nation's overarching resolution is fundamentally strengthened by the capabilities of a developed state. "With the strength of a Viksit Bengal, the resolution of a Viksit Bharat will become even stronger,” asserted Shri Modi.'
Concluding his address with deep gratitude, the Prime Minister acknowledged that the continuous affection and blessings of the people serve as an endless inspiration for public service. He offered his final felicitations for the dual celebrations of the day. "Once again, many congratulations to you all on Annapurna Diwas,” remarked Shri Modi.'

title: English rendering of PM’s remarks during the release of instalment under the Annapurna Yojana in West Bengal via video conferencing
text:
Namaskar.
My respectful greetings and regards to all mothers of Bengal!
On this special occasion, I feel immense happiness to be connected with you. I have always received great affection from the mothers and sisters of Bengal. Your trust and warmth are a great source of strength for me.
Today is also the sacred occasion of Vishwakarma Puja. I extend my heartfelt wishes to all of you on Vishwakarma Puja.
Friends,
At this auspicious time, a new tradition is being strengthened in Bengal. Today, through the Annapurna Yojana, new empowerment is being connected with the mothers and sisters of Bengal. I congratulate and send my best wishes to every sister who is benefitting from this scheme.
Friends,
In our homes, mothers and sisters carry many responsibilities. Amidst numerous small and big decisions, a woman takes care of the family in every way. And when she has less worry about essential expenses, her confidence increases even more. The Annapurna Yojana is such an important effort to strengthen the confidence of Bengal’s women. Every month, a fixed amount reaches the bank accounts of Bengal’s sisters - an amount for which they do not have to ask anyone. This is a great support in their lives.
Friends,
Today, the fourth installment of the Annapurna Yojana is reaching the accounts of nearly 15 million sisters. That means 3,000 rupees every month. For a mother, this could be the expense of her child’s education. For a sister, it could be support for medicine or essential household items.
Friends,
Our vision is that Bengal’s women should have the power to make decisions and the courage to move forward. Annapurna Yojana plays a big role in this. I extend heartfelt congratulations to all mothers and sisters who are beneficiaries of the Annapurna Yojana.
Friends,
On May 4th this year, Bengal chose a new path of transformation. And I know, in this transformation, the most important role has been played by the mothers and sisters of Bengal. You have seen many hardships in your lives. You have waited for many things. Therefore, the first test before our new government was to make the lives of Bengal’s women easier, to increase ease of living in their lives. That is why the guiding mantra we adopted was - Less talk, more work.
Friends,
The Annapurna Yojana began with this very thought. Within just a few days of forming the government, work started on this scheme. And today, money is directly reaching the bank accounts of such a large number of women. No cut money, no middlemen!
Our government’s goal is that not a single eligible woman should be deprived of the benefits of the Annapurna Yojana. Work is progressing rapidly for this too.
Friends,
Solving every problem connected with the life cycle of mothers, sisters, and daughters has been the highest priority of the BJP. To ensure nutritious food for the child during pregnancy, we launched the Matru Vandana Yojana, sending money directly to women’s bank accounts. To prevent daughters from being eliminated in the womb, we started mass movements like Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao. To ensure daughters do not drop out of school due to lack of toilets, we built millions of toilets. To continue their education, we offered high interest in the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana. To allow daughters to enter Sainik Schools, we opened their doors. To help daughters start their own work, we launched the Mudra Yojana with collateral‑free loans. To ensure mothers could continue their jobs after childbirth, we increased maternity leave. To provide new earning opportunities in villages, we gave record support to self‑help groups. To free daughters from smoke in the kitchen, we gave Ujjwala gas connections. To free them from the struggle of fetching water, we launched the Har Ghar Nal Se Jal scheme. To free them from darkness, we gave free electricity connections under the Saubhagya scheme. To ensure daughters do not hide their illness due to lack of money, we gave them the strength of the Ayushman card. To give daughters access to banks, we opened millions of accounts under Jan Dhan Yojana. To give daughters rights over property, we ensured joint ownership in PM Awas houses.
Friends,
One of Bengal’s great pains has been that in the past 12 years, many central schemes did not reach here on time. Poor families suffered the most because of this. Now, under the BJP government, these stalled schemes are being advanced rapidly. For example, the PM Awas Yojana. After the BJP government was formed in Bengal, more than 5 million new poor families have been identified to receive permanent houses under PM Awas. The PM Vishwakarma Yojana has also been implemented here. Every pending scheme, every stuck project, is now gaining new speed in Bengal. And in this, the blessings of Bengal’s women and people are with the BJP. That is why I say with great confidence - Together we will build a new Bengal.
Friends,
The nation has taken a pledge for a developed India. I am confident that Bengal’s mothers and sisters will continue to give new momentum to this journey of development. With the strength of a developed Bengal, the pledge of a developed India will become even stronger.
Friends,
Your affection, your blessings, continuously inspire us to serve. Once again, I extend many congratulations to all of you on Annapurna Day. Heartfelt wishes for Vishwakarma Puja! Thank you!
